# UI Build — Knowledge & Context

Technical reference only — no roles, no process, no review workflow. Those live in
`fedLead-playbook.md` (the role) and `fedBuild-manual.md` (the procedure).

Every claim here was measured against the installed toolchain, not inherited from an
earlier note. Beliefs that turned out to be wrong are marked **[CORRECTED]** and the
correction is kept visible rather than silently overwritten — a claim that was confidently
wrong once is worth flagging so it isn't re-derived.

*Re-verified 2026-08-25 against `develop` @ `8362b3c` (PR #59 merged) with
`feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info` checked out.*

---

## 1. How a value resolves

### The pipeline is one-way

```
theme/foundation/*.ts   ← source of truth (Tier 1)
        ↓
zimmTokens.ts           ← DERIVED. Never hand-edit.
        ↓
--zimm-* CSS custom properties
        ↓
recipes: <name>.css.ts / theme/components/*.ts
        ↓
component JSX
```

`zimmTokens.ts` imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/
`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid` from their owning files rather than
retyping values. The only literals left in it are 7 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with
no named-scale equivalent.

**A Tier 1 comment is wrong about those 7.** `theme/index.ts:47` says the 15 numeric aliases
*"are duplicates of the named scale."* `overrideStyling.md:83-85` says 7 of them are not, and
`overrideStyling.md` is right: `025` (1px), `700` (28px), `1100` (44px), `1200` (48px),
`1300` (52px), `3500` (140px), `4500` (180px) are hardcoded in `zimmTokens.ts`; the other 8
derive from `spacing`.

### The registration reality — this is the one that breaks layouts

`theme/index.ts` registers the Zimmermann scale as **`space` only** (line 56). `sizes`,
`fontSizes`, `lineHeights` and `letterSpacings` are deliberately **not** registered, because
registering them would restyle the base retail-react-app at ~199 call sites.

| Prop family | Reads | Bare key like `'xl'` |
|---|---|---|
| `margin` `padding` `gap` | `theme.space` ✅ registered | correct |
| `width` `height` `boxSize` `min/maxWidth/Height` | `theme.sizes` ❌ not registered | **falls through to Chakra's defaults** |
| `fontSize` `lineHeight` `letterSpacing` | ❌ not registered | wrong value, or nothing |

Measured blow-up range: **8×–112×**. `width: 'xl'` resolves through `theme.sizes.xl` = 36rem
= **576px** — that shipped, blew the footer contact icons to 576px, and destroyed the layout
on every page. Worse: `s`, `m`, `l` are **absent** from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
declarations are dropped entirely and silently.

Typography has the same twin. `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was intended;
`fontSize: '4xs'` emits nothing at all.

**Live unfixed instance:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:311` has `fontSize="l"`,
which emits nothing. Pre-existing, out of scope for every PR that has touched that file since.
`recipeGuards.test.ts` cannot reach it — it walks the registered recipe map only, and this is
a JSX prop. Its own `SCOPE:` note says so.

**The rule:** on a sizing or typography prop, always the CSS var —
`width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`, never `width: 'xl'`. Spacing props are fine with bare keys as
far as *correctness* goes; house style is a separate question, below.

### [CORRECTED] `var(--zimm-*)` in component JSX is now required, not a smell

An earlier revision of this document said component JSX should use `textStyle` plus semantic
token strings (`color="text.default"`, `padding="m"`), and that seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was
a signal to look closer. **That is inverted from the current rule and following it now fails
review.**

`overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2 and `css.md` both state it plainly:

```tsx
// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ the raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

The stated reason is **house style, not correctness**: a bare key resolves to the identical
value on a registered scale, but it forces a reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s
registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. A `var()` reference is
unambiguous at every call site.

`textStyle` is the one legitimate bare key — there is no `var()` for the composite expansion,
only for its individual pieces.

**And it can never emit one.** `zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts`, so the reverse
would be a circular import; `textStyle` therefore always expands to resolved literals at build
time. **This is correct behaviour, not a defect** — and it means roughly **85% of what an
emitted-CSS audit flags as "raw literals" is `textStyle` working as designed.** Read any
`audit:tokens` output with that in mind.

**What survives from the old advice, and is still the main point:** brand values mostly should
not be in JSX at all. Measured on `develop` 2026-08-25 — `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **14
theme files on `develop`** (10 co-located `<name>.css.ts` + 4 under `theme/components/`) — 18 in
the current working tree, which adds four uncommitted product-view recipes — and in exactly
**one** component `.tsx`: `footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62`, a conditional
`paddingLeft` that no Chakra prop expresses. So the practice is: type via `textStyle`,
colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine prop-system gap.

**Live violations right now:** `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductName/index.tsx:20` and
`zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:23` both use `color="text.default"`.

### Value equality is not token equality

Before replacing a literal with a token, three checks — all three must pass:

1. **Same unit?** `rem` and `px` are not interchangeable. Swapping `3rem` for a px-defined
   alias is a **WCAG 1.4.4 regression**, not a tidy-up.
2. **Same semantic scale?** A spacing value and a sizing value that happen to be equal are not
   the same token.
3. **Is the target permitted?** The numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases are **class-only** —
   never in JSX or a recipe.

Three real false positives died on these: `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` → `--zimm-scale-1200`
(check 1), `SIZE_COL_NAV` (check 2), and `SIZE_MODAL_SUB` ≡ `breakpoints.sm`, which was pure
coincidence.

### The real invariant is single-sourcing, not `var()` syntax

Ask of any value: *is this typed more than once?* Not: *is this a `var()`?* An audit built on
syntax generates mostly noise.

PR #56 reduced `foundation/`'s hand-typed literals from 237 to 64 — **173 were duplicates**,
the same `24px` appearing in `typography.ts` and again in `zimmTokens.ts`. Two later PRs
recreated that duplication one layer up without noticing: PR #52 hand-rebuilt in `sx` what
`textStyle="heading3"` already gave, five times; PR #55 added `cssVars.ts`, 241 lines mirroring
`zimmTokens.ts`'s keys as `var()` strings plus a reimplementation of seven registered text
styles. It was removed — a 245-line deletion; at its peak it had 10 consumer files and 148 references.

Both misreads passed CodeRabbit. It confirmed every correctness finding and raised **zero**
architecture findings.

### Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with root font-size or browser zoom (WCAG 1.4.4) —
  type and spacing. Sub-pixel letter-spacing values keep a trailing `// -0.12px` comment for
  traceability, since they don't round to clean rem.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should *not* scale — border widths, focus-ring offsets.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts`, deliberate so media queries shift with zoom)
  and other genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

---

## 2. Chakra behaviours that fail silently

Seven mechanisms. None produces an error, a warning, or a failing type-check.

**0. Always declare your own `parts` array.** A recipe with no `parts` inherits the base's
list, so any Zimmermann part you add is undeclared and silently unstyled.

**1. `extendTheme` deep-merges — it does not replace.** A recipe named `Footer` merges into
base SFCC's `Footer` rather than replacing it, inheriting parts you never wrote. Namespace
everything: `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`. `recipeGuards.test.ts` enforces this with
`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — those three are deliberate; anything
else must be namespaced.

**1b. The merge reorders keys.** A key that already exists in the base keeps the **base's**
position in the merged object; a key you add that the base lacks is appended **last**. That is
the mechanism behind a shorthand resetting a longhand you wrote first — the order in your file
is not the order that ships. Inspect what actually applies:

```js
theme.components.Header.baseStyle   // merged — what actually applies
```

**2. A recipe unit test cannot catch the merge.** `extendTheme` does **not** populate
`theme.__cssMap` — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`. So a direct `css()(theme)`
assertion in Vitest passes vacuously against an unmerged object.

**3. Compound values never tokenise.** Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value.
`padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser. Use axis props
(`paddingInline`, `paddingBlock`).

**4. A shorthand declared after a longhand resets it.** `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock`
wipes it. Order matters; prefer the axis props throughout.

**5. `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"`** as a style prop, merged *after* `__css`, so a `p:`
in your recipe size is discarded. **Size it with `minW`/`minH`** — which is also how you hit the
24×24 target-size requirement.

**6. Register the recipe or destructuring throws at runtime.** Chakra resolves a recipe by the
string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path — so co-location is free, but the
key must be in `theme/components/index.ts`.

**7. Breakpoint tokens conflict with Chakra's.** `BP.desktop` is 64em; Chakra's `lg` is 62em
and `xl` is 80em. A responsive array silently steps at the wrong width. Write explicit media
queries:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

The array shorthand also puts a bare token key at every step, and the guard flags all four.

---

## 3. Component structure

### Placement — settled

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx
```

Being under `components/` is load-bearing for the registry generator, which scans that path.

**Three casing families, each correct in its own context. Do not generalise between them:**

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | must match upstream's import path |
| ui-kit component | `zimmButton/` camelCase | Zimmermann-authored — the default rule |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | mirrors upstream exactly |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Note the theme key is
PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`) while its recipe file is camelCase.

### Tier is by composition, not visual size

Read it off the imports, not the DOM:

- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit. `zimmModal` is an atom despite being portal + backdrop +
  `role="dialog"` chrome, because it owns no content (`maxWidth`, `labelledBy`, children all
  come from the caller).
- **molecule** — composes atoms with light local logic. `zimmInputAction` = TextInput + Button
  + local validation state.
- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**. `zimmSubscribeSection`
  owns the subscribe state machine.

An icon passed as a prop doesn't count (`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom). Slotted
children don't count.

**Storybook `title` is a different axis from the folder.** Folder = composition depth;
`title` = domain. `zimmModal` (atom) → `Elements/`; `zimmSubscribeSection` (organism) →
`Forms/`; `Footer` → `Layout/`. Don't conflate them.

### Styling surface — a registered recipe, always

Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a plain stylesheet. The recipe may live beside
the component as `<name>.css.ts` or centrally in `theme/components/` — Chakra resolves by
string key, so this is purely organisational.

The argument against authoring in a stylesheet is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see
`var(--zimm-*)`, which is **derived output at the bottom of the pipeline**. Author there and
you lose `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, and the theme
drift-guard tests. Not bad CSS — the wrong end of the pipeline.

For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is the bridge:
native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`.

**Co-location changes who reviews it.** `CODEOWNERS:186`
(`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only) is placed **last** among the
`components/` rules, and CODEOWNERS is last-match-wins, not most-specific-wins. So a `.css.ts`
inside `footer/` drops the Tier 2 approver requirement the surrounding directory carries,
while `footer/index.tsx` keeps it. The stated rationale: a co-located recipe *composes
established tokens*; authoring a new token still means `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1).

`overrideStyling.md` flags its own inconsistency here rather than papering over it —
`zimmButton.css.ts` keys the app-wide `Button` recipe and is no longer designer-gated.

### No data-fetching in `components/`

Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props. Data-fetching belongs in
`overrides/app/pages/` or a container.

**One documented exception:** Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`,
`useUiCopy`) may be called from any component including presentational leaves, because they
read from a Provider mounted above the route tree. Narrow by design — content identical for
every consumer regardless of route, not anything that varies per page.

**Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades:
`useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`, one line, renders with zero setup. **`useIntl`
throws** (`invariantIntlContext`), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the base SFCC `_app`,
not `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. Any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer
must wrap it.

### Two API patterns worth copying

- **Encode the a11y contract in a discriminated union** so an inaccessible combination doesn't
  type-check.
- **Make an absent affordance opt-in**, not a silent default.

### Do not trust the registry's tier column

`generateRegistry.mjs:125-203` hardcodes tier arrays, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults
everything else to Tier 4. The registry is auto-generated and its *paths* are reliable; its
*tier* column is not.

### What is actually overridden today [CORRECTED]

An earlier revision said **seven** directories. It is now **eleven**:

```
_app-config  button  contentful  footer  foundation  header
icons  pageContainer  product-view  ui-kits  uiCopyProvider
```

`footer/` is a full override with three co-located recipes. Two organisms exist
(`zimmSubscribeModal`, `zimmSubscribeSection`) where an earlier note said none did.
`theme/components/button.ts` no longer exists — it is
`ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`. `theme/components/` now holds only
`footerShared.ts`, `header.ts`, `index.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts`,
`recipeGuards.test.ts`.

Still base, despite being referenced throughout `.claude/rules/`: `product-tile`,
`display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu`, `seo`.
**Assume most stories pay copy-first**, and expect a rules file's worked example not to exist.

---

## 4. What an override actually intercepts

Three silent failure modes. In each, the override compiles, resolves, and never runs.

**1. The resolver is webpack-only.** `ccExtensibility` in `package.json` redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` in the **real app build only**.
`.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to `node_modules`, and `vitest.config.ts`
doesn't touch it. So a base-path import of an already-overridden component builds correctly in
the shipped app and silently renders the **unstyled base version** in Storybook and Vitest —
the story looks like it's exercising your override and isn't.

When importing a component that already has an override, use a **relative path**
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the base path.

**2. A relative barrel re-export is not rewritten.** The attractive play — override
`shared/ui/<Name>` so branded styling propagates into base cart, checkout and account for free
— **does not work.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` does `export {Button} from './Button'`, a
relative export the resolver does not rewrite. And the consumption pattern is the wrong way
round: **212 base files import the barrel (195 excluding tests); 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.** The override
intercepts nothing.

**3. A conditional render of an alternate module.** Overriding a component doesn't help if the
parent renders something else on that route. `footer` never reaches `/checkout`.

**The generalised check**, before scoping any story around "override X and it propagates":

```bash
grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

### The SFCC bridge pattern

If a component is used internally by SFCC's own base components, its **default export must
stay a faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour.
Put Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps it.

⚠️ **No worked precedent exists in this repo.** `product-tile` is still base, `CardBaseline`
returns zero hits across `overrides/`, and `grep -rn forwardRef overrides/` returns one file.
Whoever needs this pattern first will be establishing it, not copying it.

Where token-driven theming suffices, a theme recipe is preferable to a second export — the
prop-narrowing that motivated `CardBaseline` isn't needed for styling alone.

---

## 5. Figma to code

### The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,
  `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts:
  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — a delta here is a
  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against 45/68 was a real gap, and a naive
  "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one
is a defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the
heading's cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.css.ts`, deriving from
`lineHeight` + 4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

### There are two Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like

`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page
file produced two wrong conclusions in a row — first "the slot is 59px in both states"
(actually `Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap
change 40→24: the design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix
that suppressed intended growth when the 68px padded box was already correct.

### Frames are not breakpoints

Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024. The unframed **768–1022
band was genuinely broken** — 18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels — and covers three iPad
models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking*: the row refused to
break, so the words broke instead.

### Type metrics

The fallback stack renders roughly **13% wider** than Futura Round, which is why serving the
real faces matters for parity review. `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable
families and is useless — compare widths instead.

### Measurement method

**Subtract non-component bands before comparing totals** — the footer compares against 476,
not 606, once the `Disclaimer` band is excluded. **Isolate causes by cumulative in-DOM
mutation, one candidate at a time.** Measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports
frame-relative coordinates). Use
`domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server. Dismiss the consent banner first.
`Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point. **Mutation-test layout
fixes at mobile** — two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only because a taller sibling column masked
them.

**A design nudge is still spec.** Ship it and raise the question — don't silently "correct"
it, and don't silently ignore it. Document the deviation at the point of use.

### No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect

`width: 'xl'` resolving to 576px destroyed the footer on every page while passing `tsc`,
`eslint`, `vitest`, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and the Storybook a11y run. Only rendering
beside Figma found it.

---

## 6. Layout mechanics

Six mechanisms, each with the fix that actually worked.

1. **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line.** `width: min-content`
   resolves to the widest unbreakable run — usually what you want when a column should hug its
   longest word rather than its container.

2. **`minHeight` plus `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps.** The centring
   discards the extra line's leading rather than growing the box. Derive height from
   `lineHeight` plus padding instead of reserving a `minHeight`.

3. **An inline child inside a block parent leaks descender space.** A block-level `<li>`
   wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` gets a line box whose strut sits below the baseline —
   measured **25.5px against the anchor's own 24px**, leaking 1.5px per row (3px on a wrapped
   label) and making the footer's links column 9px taller than Figma's 158px.
   **Fix: `display: flex` on the `<li>`**, which removes the line box entirely.
   `footerNavColumn.css.ts:69` is the shipped instance.
   ⚠️ `display: block` is the **bug**, not the fix.

4. **Give the gap to the heading, not the column.** If the design nests a group inside a stack
   with no gap, don't reproduce it as a sibling in a gapped flex container — the container's
   gap then applies where the design has none. Put the spacing on the heading's `marginBottom`.

5. **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking.** The row refuses to break, so the
   words break instead. This is what broke the unframed 768–1022 band.

6. **A non-breaking space must be the `\u00A0` escape**, not a literal character in source —
   invisible to review and unpredictable under reformatting. Note the dependency it creates:
   production copy has to carry the same character.

**A solution window measured in single pixels is a coincidence, not a tolerance.** The footer's
viable column cap was **[131, 132.9) — 1.9px wide**. Treat that as a signal the constraint set
is over-determined, not as a fix that happens to work.

## 7. Building against absent data

### Three patterns, only the first correct

**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
promised; never render a control that can't act.

- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that
  **keeps its margins**, measured as a roughly 64px void. It doesn't collapse; it reserves
  space for nothing.
- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.

### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build

Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:

| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |

The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).

The same treatment is reused three times for "control with no action": the contact fallback,
`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).

### Never branch on localised CMS text

`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.

### Guarding hrefs

Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**

---

## 8. CMS data and the tier reality

New section. The footer rendered correctly in dev and was blank on the test tier, and nothing
in the component was wrong.

### Content types and entries promote by different mechanisms

| | Content **types** (schema) | Content (**entries**) |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | org-scoped Environment Template | *nothing automated* |
| Build | `npm run sync:contentful` | — |
| Deploy | `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` | — |

**A template cannot carry entries — this is structural.** The SDK type has exactly two slots:

```ts
// contentful-management/dist/types/entities/environment-template.d.ts:31-34
entities: {
    contentTypeTemplates: Array<ContentTypeTemplateProps>;
    editorInterfaceTemplates: Array<EditorInterfaceTemplateProps>;
};
```

No `entries`, no `assets`. The only entry-writing code in the repo is `seedRegions.mjs:71-72`,
which handles the 11 `region` entries and nothing else.

### Verified tier state, 2026-08-25

| tier | content types | published entries |
|---|---|---|
| **dev** | **14** | **42** (+3 assets) |
| test / sit / uat / staging | **0** | **0** |
| prod | no environment id configured | — |

The environments exist — the CDA returned `total: 0`, not `NotFound`. Nothing has ever been
promoted out of dev.

**The template covers 5 of dev's 14 types** — `footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`,
`region`, `uiCopy`. The other 9 exist only inside the dev environment, UI-authored, with no
code representation, and `install:contentful` cannot move them.

**There is no forward content promotion in this repo at all.** The actual release model is the
alias flip in `promoteAlias.mjs`: clone master → install template → author and verify →
repoint `production`/`master`. Content moves *backwards* (master → clone), never forwards.

### Fetch-depth is load-bearing

`include: 3` is not arbitrary. At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved stubs,
`region.fields.siteId` throws, the `.catch` swallows it, and the **entire footer renders
nothing**. A resolution-depth mistake looks identical to a network failure from the page.

### Locale is not passed on any Contentful fetch

`useContentful.ts:110` builds a URL with `content_type`, `access_token` and `include` only, so
the footer and `uiCopy` get the space default on all eight storefronts. Three invocation sites
across two production files. (`pages/experience/` and `pages/contentfulPreview/` *do* pass
`localeCode` — the gap is the shared hook, not every caller.) Blocked on a shared-
hook signature change, which is a team RFC.

### The check to run before promising a component works on a tier

```bash
curl -s "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/<space>/environments/<env>/entries?content_type=<type>&limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <that tier's delivery token>"
```

`total: 1` means it will render. `unknownContentType` means the model was never installed.
Note the CDA returns an unreliable `total` at `limit=0` — use `limit=1`.

---

## 9. Accessibility patterns

Six recurring success criteria and what each actually demanded.

- **1.1.1** — a degraded control must stay *labelled*, not `aria-hidden`. Silence is
  information loss.
- **1.4.4 / 1.4.10** — `rem` for anything that must survive zoom; a modal panel needs
  `maxHeight` + `overflowY` or tall content centres half-off-screen and is unreachable.
- **2.4.4 / 3.2.4** — no `href` and no `tabIndex` on a control that cannot act, so nothing
  promises an action that can't be performed.
- **2.5.8** — 24×24 minimum target size, which is a WCAG **2.2** addition and easy to miss if
  working from a 2.1 checklist.
- **2.5.3 Label in name** — the accessible name must *contain* the visible label.
- **3.2.5** — a link leaving the site gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a suffix in its
  accessible name. That is the project's external-link standard; it lives nowhere else.
- **Focus** — a programmatic `.focus()` does **not** match `:focus-visible`. A focus ring
  styled only on `:focus-visible` will not appear after a scripted focus move.
- **Portal + focus trap** — when `activeElement` is outside the trap, the trap must handle it
  rather than assume containment.

Every `IconButton` needs `aria-label`; every `<img>` needs `alt` (`alt=""` for decorative).
Note the ast-grep rule matches `^img$` only, so Chakra's `<Image>` is invisible to it, and its
`aria-label` check does not match `aria-labelledby`.

---

## 10. Verification: what actually proves anything

### The integrity principle

> The verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it verified, and was
> never made to fail on purpose.

That is the single recurring failure mode. A green check that was never proven capable of going
red carries no information.

Catalogued instances, all self-caught after reporting a false all-clear: a `safeHref` suite
reported "well covered, 3 layers" whose 13 cases contained **zero backslashes** — the exact
vector already named; a `fontFace` test iterating an empty array; a mutation test that
"passed" because `perl -pi` works line-at-a-time and cannot match `\n`; a recipe parity check
that false-alarmed three times on recipes whose `baseStyle` is a **function**; a literal-count
sweep that inflated 19→41 by matching `.rem` inside `removeEventListener`.

### Copy the non-vacuity meta-test

`recipeGuards.test.ts` includes `test('collect() actually walks the registered recipes')`
precisely because every other guard asserts `toEqual([])`, which an empty input satisfies.
Stubbing `components` to `{}` turned the whole file green — verified.

Same shape for layout assertions: a pure before/after equality is satisfied vacuously by a
collapsed container (`display:none`, `height:0`, an ancestor `display:none` — and every rect
is 0 in jsdom). **Anchor the measurement above zero first.**

And resolve a function-form `baseStyle` across **all** boolean prop combinations, not the
default one. The original bug hid down a conditional branch a single-resolution walk never
entered.

### Green tests that encode the bug

A suite can test *around* a defect. The region tie-break suite had a case named "order of the
tied candidates does not change the outcome" that used only **distinct** timestamps — the one
arrangement already order-independent. It passed while the bug was live.

Mutation testing is necessary but not sufficient: it proves the check *can* fail, not that it
fails for the right reason.

### [CORRECTED] What is and is not gated

**a11y IS gated.** An earlier belief — repeated four times in one session and again by a fresh
analysis this week — was that a11y is ungated because there is no `.storybook/test-runner.js`.
**That is Storybook 8 knowledge and is wrong for what is installed.**
`@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`'s `dist/setup-page-script.js:390-397` reads
`story.parameters?.a11y?.test` and throws when it `=== "error"`; `.storybook/preview.tsx:44`
sets exactly that. No `test-runner.js` is needed. **Do not delete that `preview.tsx` block.**

Honest rider: the gate has never been made to fail on purpose, so by the standard above it is
**unproven, not absent**.

**Gated nowhere at all:** `eslint`, `prettier`, `tsc --noEmit`, `audit:tokens`, any CSS bundle
budget, test coverage. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide on pre-existing prettier errors
and CI never notices.

**A skipped required check counts as passing.** Live on PR #59: all four suites reported
`skipping` — including both *required* checks — while `mergeable: true`. `detect-changes` uses
`since_last_remote_commit`, and a final push touching only registry files fell outside every
allow-list. A 93-commit PR became merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**.
Read `gh pr checks` for `skipping`, not just for green.

**A named gate that cannot fail:** `npm run test:contracts` is `echo 'TODO…' && exit 0`, and
it is a hard `needs` of `sit-gate`.

### Harness traps

- **`test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.** Dev-server runs made four mutation results
  uninterpretable.
- **Vitest does not run `play`.**
- **jsdom always provides `window`**, so an SSR branch needs `// @vitest-environment node`.
- **Every jsdom rect is 0** — layout assertions there are meaningless.
- **`ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel, whose top-level
  `AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...` fails because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings here.
  Unfixable from a test file (`vitest.config.ts` is Tier 1). Mock at the smallest surface:
  ```ts
  vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))
  ```
  …or forward `aria-label`/`aria-hidden` when an assertion depends on the accessible name.
- **Portalled content is scoped to `document.body`, not `canvasElement`.** `canvasElement` is
  `#storybook-root`, a *sibling* of the portal target. Measured: `canvasElement.innerHTML` is
  41 characters, 0 dialogs inside the canvas against 1 in the document. A canvas-scoped
  `getByRole` fails immediately; `findByRole` fails after ~1002ms; the body-scoped form passes
  in 1–2ms. `testing.md:128`'s "never reach into `document`" has no portal carve-out — that is
  a documentation defect, not a code one.
- **`@storybook/test` is not installed.** `testing.md:115` prescribes it; Storybook 10 moved it
  to `storybook/test`. Following that line verbatim breaks.

### The gap no tool covers

Duplication and reuse. No tool detects "this is a second Button." Nothing catches a bare token
key used as a JSX prop. Nothing catches a layout defect. Nothing catches a component whose data
doesn't exist on the tier it ships to.

---

## 11. Signposts in the repo that point at nothing

Each of these has already cost time.

- **`overrides.md` does not exist.** `overrideStyling.md:4,112,179` references it three times
  and positions it as the companion doc defining module-replacement correctness. It exists only
  on two unmerged spike branches.
- **`overrideStyling.md` is orphaned and unsynced.** `AGENTS.md` never references it
  (`grep -c` → 0). `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`'s manifest omits it, along with `css.md`,
  `components.md`, `typescript.md` and `tagging.md` — three of which are in `conventions.md`'s
  own "See also" list. The largest rules file, holding the entire styling hierarchy, is
  invisible to Cursor and Copilot.
- **The rules set is split on its own component convention.** `components.md` and
  `conventions.md` contain **zero** occurrences of `ui-kits`, `atoms`, `molecules` or
  `organisms`. `new-component/SKILL.md:29` still scaffolds to the flat path.
  `.docs/architecture.md` contradicts itself — `:136` cites the correct
  `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` while `:130`/`:139` prescribe a
  `components/custom/` directory that has never existed.
- **[CORRECTED] `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` now exists.** Earlier notes said it didn't. It
  was built 2026-08-23 and `npm run audit:tokens` is wired. It is still **not in CI** — a
  current run reports **19 unacknowledged violations**, 14 pre-existing plus 5 in
  `product-view/index.tsx`.
- **`test:lighthouse` is broken.** `package.json:57` points at `tests/lighthouserc.js`; the
  real file is `./lighthouserc.js` and there is no `tests/` directory. CI is unaffected —
  `digital-sit.yml` runs bare `lhci autorun`, which auto-discovers. `AGENTS.md:37` names the
  same dead path.
- **`deploy-dev.yml`'s `tag-sprint` job reads `scripts/sprint.txt`**, which does not exist and
  never has. The job runs on every dev deploy and is a guarded permanent no-op — no sprint tag
  has ever been created.
- **`squadA.md` and `squadB.md` are largely fiction.** Of squadA's 21 territory paths, 4 exist;
  **zero** of squadB's 9 do. Both instruct edits to files not in the repo, and both were last
  touched 2026-07-14. And they contradict `CODEOWNERS` on PDP ownership —
  CODEOWNERS says Squad B and is the one that enforces.
- **`sprintScope.md` is two months stale** and `AGENTS.md` Hard Rule 14 makes it load-bearing
  for scoping. It says "Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress)" while its own table puts today in
  Sprint 5. Applied literally it would classify current PDP work as past-sprint.
- **`.docs/architecture.md` misstates the stack**: React Router v6 (actually 5.3.4 — the
  footer uses `useHistory`), Storybook 8 (actually 10.4.6), axe via `vitest-axe`/`axe-playwright`
  (neither installed), Playwright "not yet configured" (7 projects, two workflows), "all
  services mocked (MSW stubs)" — `msw@1.3.5` is present transitively but has zero references in
  `overrides/`, and it is a test tool, not a local-dev data source. (`AGENTS.md` bans MSW in
  *production paths* only; `testing.md` permits it for integration tests.)
- **`CONTENT_TYPE_IDS`** (`overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts:53` — note the top-level
  `config/` is a different, Tier 1 directory) has zero consumers and duplicates
  `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js`.
- **`connectionPools.ts` looks like live infrastructure and is dead code** — `ssr.js` doesn't
  import it. The blast-radius isolation its header claims is not in effect.

**The pattern:** trust the code, `CODEOWNERS`, `recipeGuards.test.ts`, and `tagging.md`.
Verify everything else before citing it. A rules file's worked example is as likely to describe
an unmerged branch as the one you're on.

---

*Compiled 2026-08-25 from the SFCC-55 global-footer build (PR #59, 93 commits, merged
2026-08-24) and the Contentful tier investigation that followed it. Claims re-measured against
the installed toolchain rather than inherited. Five beliefs that were confidently wrong are
marked [CORRECTED] — most consequentially the `var(--zimm-*)` hierarchy, which had inverted
without any of these notes noticing, and the a11y gate, which exists and was twice reported
absent.*

17	## 1. The Operating Principles
18	
19	### Static-first
20	
21	Props in, markup out. A component under `overrides/app/components/` receives its data and
22	renders it. It does not fetch.
23	
24	Mock data goes in the story — never a temporary fetch you intend to remove. A component that
25	owns its own data-fetching cannot be reused where the data arrives differently: SSR-prefetched,
26	mocked in Storybook, or composed by a parent that already has it.
27	
28	**The one exception**, and it is narrow: Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks
29	(`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called from any component, including a presentational leaf.
30	They read from a Provider mounted above the route tree, so they don't create the
31	SSR/Storybook/composition problem the rule exists to prevent. This covers content identical for
32	every consumer regardless of route — not anything that varies per page.
33	
34	⚠️ **Their no-Provider behaviour differs and it will bite you in tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades
35	to fallback text and renders with zero setup. **`useIntl` throws**, and its `IntlProvider` is
36	mounted by the base SFCC `_app`, not `_app-config` — a narrower subtree than you'd expect. Any
37	Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer must wrap it.
38	
39	### Leverage what already exists
40	
41	Four rungs, in order:
42	
43	1. **Use the base SFCC component as-is.**
44	2. **Override it** — mirror the path under `overrides/`, keep the kebab-case filename.
45	
46	**The default is override, not build — because an override inherits the wiring for free.**
47	Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the
48	add-to-cart modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. And because the
49	resolver rewires imports transparently, overriding a component that SFCC's own base components
50	import means **the entire base template inherits your version with zero call sites touched**.
51	
52	Worked examples: size selector → `swatch-group`; add to bag → `product-view`; max quantity →
53	`quantity-picker`; variant resolution → `use-controlled-variations` / `use-derived-product`.
54	Check what the base already does before scoping — a ticket saying "Cart API integration is in
55	scope" may be describing a call the base already makes.
56	3. **Compose existing ui-kit atoms** into something new.
57	4. **Build a new component.** Rarest. Justify it.
58	
59	Before rung 4, check the registry (`.claude/registry/`) and grep `ui-kits/`.
60	
61	**What `shared/ui` is actually for:** Contentful renderers need *primitives*, not commerce
62	components. Every Contentful component on `develop` already pulls them in — `duplexSection`
63	(`Box`, `Text`), `collectionHero` (`Box`, `Button`, `Heading`, `Text`), `hotspotPopup`,
64	`imageText`, `heroBanner`. Upstream those resolve to bare Chakra.

66	⚠️ **But the barrel is not the leverage play it looks like.** Overriding
67	`shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate branded styling into base cart/checkout/account **does not
68	work** — `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite,
69	and 212 base files import the barrel (195 excluding tests) while **0** import the individual module. See
70	`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §4.

73	
74	Not at the end. **And check the Jira card's Figma link actually points at your frame** — a
75	stale link propagates: you build the wrong thing, the BA signs off against a different frame,
76	QA tests a third source. If it's wrong, ask the BA to fix the card rather than working it out
77	in a DM.
78	
79	There are **two Figma files** and cross-comparing them produces confident nonsense. See
80	`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §5.

84	Roughly 30 minutes stuck is the trigger. One question at a time.

88	The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3** — the whole project, not per sprint. (Contract figure;

95	## 2. Before you write any code
96	
97	### Confirm the branch
98	
99	```bash
100	git branch --show-current
101	```
102	
103	If it's `develop` or `main`, stop. No changes.

106	
107	Read `.claude/registry/` for the component. The `Origin` column is what matters:
108	
109	| Origin | Means |
110	|---|---|
111	| `Custom` | Zimmermann-authored, already here |
112	| `Override` | already mirrored into `overrides/` |
113	| **`Base`** | **still upstream — you pay copy-first** |
114

116	arrays, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything else to Tier 4. Paths are reliable;

118

120	
121	| Family | Casing | Example |
122	|---|---|---|
123	| SFCC override | kebab-case, matching upstream exactly | `product-tile/` |
124	| **ui-kit component** | **camelCase — the default for new work** | `zimmButton/` |
125	| `shared/ui` primitive | PascalCase, mirroring upstream | `Button/` |

132

137	  <name>.css.ts          ← the recipe
138	  index.test.tsx         ← if it has branching or event wiring
139	```
140	
141	**Tier by composition, read off the imports:**
142	
143	- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit
144	- **molecule** — composes atoms, light local state
145	- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**
146	
147	An icon passed as a prop doesn't count. Slotted children don't count.
148	
149	### What's actually overridden today
150	
151	Eleven directories:
152	
153	```
154	_app-config  button  contentful  footer  foundation  header
155	icons  pageContainer  product-view  ui-kits  uiCopyProvider
156	```
157	
158	Still base, despite being referenced throughout `.claude/rules/`: `product-tile`,
159	`display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu`, `seo`.
160	**Assume most stories pay copy-first.**
161	
162	### The copy-first rule
163	
164	For any task requiring an override that doesn't exist yet, prepare **all of them at once**
165	before any functional change:
166	
167	1. Copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path.
168	2. Convert to `.ts`/`.tsx`, update imports.
169	3. `npx tsc --noEmit`.
170	4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` to each.
171	5. **Stop.** Let the user confirm the overrides are rendering.
172	6. Remove the `console.log`s, then make functional changes.
173	
174	Never bundle this silently with functional work.

178	## 3. Design Foundations
179	
180	*The longest section, and the part that moves. Read it before your first component.*
181	
182	### The styling hierarchy
183	
184	1. **`textStyle`** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`. All 22
185	   Handover text styles are registered:
186	
187	   `heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong`
188	   `body2` · `mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg`
189	   `linkSm` · `button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif`
190	2. **`var(--zimm-*)`** for colour and spacing. The spacing scale:
191	
192	   | | | | | | | |
193	   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
194	   | `3xs` 2px | `2xs` 4px | `xs` 8px | `s` 12px | `m` 16px | `l` 20px | `xl` 24px |
195	   | `2xl` 32px | `3xl` 40px | `4xl` 64px | `5xl` 80px | `6xl` 128px | `7xl` 160px | |
196	
197	   Semantic colour groups in `foundation/colour.ts`: `background` (01–07), `text`, `border`,
198	   `status`, `link`, `icon`, `action` (`primary.*`, `secondary.*`).
199	3. **The component's own recipe** for anything varying by variant/size/state.
200	4. **`sx`** for a one-off prop-system gap.
201	5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it. In practice: never. There is
202	   no `.scss` anywhere in the footer or `ui-kits`.
203	
204	### ⚠️ [CORRECTED] Rung 2 inverted — bare token strings are now wrong
205	
206	An earlier revision of this manual taught `color="text.default"` and `padding="m"`, and said
207	seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was a smell. **That is backwards from the current rule.**
208	
209	```tsx
210	// ❌ bare Chakra/theme token string in an override component
211	<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />
212	
213	// ✅ raw var(--zimm-*) reference
214	<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
215	```
216	
217	⚠️ **Two different rules are in play and it's easy to conflate them.** A bare key on a *spacing*
218	prop is **correct but against house style** — `theme.space` is registered, so it resolves. A bare
219	key on a *sizing or typography* prop is **broken** — those scales aren't registered at all. The
220	first gets a review comment; the second ships a 576px icon.
221	
222	The reason is **house style, not correctness** — a bare key resolves identically, but forces a
223	reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it's correct.
224	
225	`textStyle` stays a bare key. It's the one exception: there's no `var()` for the composite.
226	
227	**In practice this rarely arises**, because brand values mostly shouldn't be in JSX at all.
228	Measured on `develop`: `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **18 recipe files** and exactly **one**
229	component `.tsx` — a conditional `paddingLeft` no Chakra prop expresses. Type via `textStyle`,
230	colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine gap.
231	
232	### Icon, action and motion values are constants, not theme tokens
233	
234	They collide with Chakra's scales the same way — `theme.sizes.lg` is 32rem and backs `boxSize`
235	everywhere — so they are **imported directly** rather than registered:
236	
237	```tsx
238	import { iconSizes, actionSizes, motion } from 'app/theme/foundation';
239	
240	<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />            // 20px
241	<Button height={actionSizes.height.lg} />  // 52px
242	```
243	
244	| | |
245	|---|---|
246	| `iconSizes` | `lg` 20px · `md` 16px · `sm` 12px |
247	| `actionSizes` | `height.{lg: 52, md: 40}` · `paddingX.{lg: 32, md: 20}` · `gap: 16` |
248	| `motion` | `duration.{fast: 200, default: 300, slow: 500}ms` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}` |
249	
250	⚠️ **Motion values are PROVISIONAL**, pending designer sign-off — `motion.ts` says so itself.
251	
252	`borderWidth.default` is 1px. `focusRingOffsets.default` is 2px, `.secondary` 3px — the second
253	exists to clear the secondary button's 1px border.
254	
255	### ⚠️ The trap: a spacing key on a sizing prop
256	
257	**This shipped a completely broken footer, so it's worth being blunt about.**
258	
259	```tsx
260	padding: 'xl',   // ✅ reads theme.space.xl
261	width: 'xl',     // ❌ reads theme.sizes.xl = 36rem = 576px
262	```
263	
264	Only `space` is registered. `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` are not.
265	Measured blow-up range **8×–112×**. And `s`/`m`/`l` are absent from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
266	declarations are **dropped silently**.
267	
268	Nothing catches this. `'xl'` is a valid `SystemStyleObject` value so TypeScript is satisfied,
269	no lint rule exists, and no test asserts layout. It passed `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`,
270	CodeRabbit (local *and* PR) and the Storybook a11y run — only rendering the page found it.
271	
272	`recipeGuards.test.ts` now guards it **inside recipes**. It cannot see a JSX prop.
273	
274	### ⚠️ `extendTheme` MERGES — it does not replace
275	
276	Name a recipe `Footer` and it deep-merges into base SFCC's `Footer`, inheriting parts you never
277	wrote. Namespace everything: `ZimmFooter`.
278	
279	`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — those three are deliberate. Anything
280	else must be namespaced, and `recipeGuards.test.ts` fails the build if it isn't.
281	
282	⚠️ A recipe unit test **cannot catch this**: `extendTheme` doesn't populate `theme.__cssMap`,
283	only `ChakraProvider` does. A direct `css()(theme)` assertion passes vacuously.
284	
285	### Responsive steps are explicit media queries
286	
287	```ts
288	[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: {
289	  flexDirection: 'row',
290	  padding: `var(--zimm-scale-4xl) var(--zimm-scale-3xl) ${SPACE_SECTION}`,
291	},
292	```
293	
294	Two reasons. The array shorthand (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) puts a bare token key at every
295	step and the guard flags all four. And `BP.desktop` (64em) **conflicts with Chakra's `lg`=62em
296	/ `xl`=80em**, so a responsive prop silently steps at the wrong width.
297	
298	### Register the recipe or it throws
299	
300	Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path.
301	Co-location is therefore free — but the key must be in `theme/components/index.ts` or
302	destructuring throws at runtime.
303	
304	**A registered recipe nothing reads is dead code.** Chakra's `<Button>`/`<Link>` read theirs
305	automatically; a custom multipart component must call `useMultiStyleConfig` (or `useStyleConfig`
306	for a single-part one). A registered-but-unread recipe looks like compliance and changes nothing.
307	
308	The consumption pattern is always three lines:
309	
310	```ts
311	const ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooter';
312	const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE, {});
313	```
314	
315	### Interaction state belongs in CSS, not React state
316	
317	`_hover`, `_active`, `_focusVisible`, `_disabled` in the recipe. Not `useState` + `onMouseEnter`.
318	It looks identical in a screenshot and behaves differently in five ways that all matter:
319	touch devices, keyboard focus, rapid pointer movement, SSR output, and re-render cost.
320	
321	⚠️ A programmatic `.focus()` does **not** match `:focus-visible`. A ring styled only on
322	`:focus-visible` won't appear after a scripted focus move.
323	
324	### `.zimm-*` global classes
325	
326	~28 classes live in `globalStyles.ts` — `.zimm-text-*`, `.zimm-form-*`, `.zimm-grid`,
327	`.zimm-focus-visible`. They ship on **every page** and have almost no consumers today (one
328	Storybook demo uses `.zimm-grid`).
329	
330	**There are no `.zimm-btn-*` classes, and there must never be.** A component with both a class
331	and a recipe has two surfaces that drift. Use Chakra's `<Button>`.
332	
333	Don't reach for a class for new work — a registered recipe, always. The classes remain
334	defensible only for genuinely static, non-interactive, massively-reused treatments.
335	
336	### You don't add tokens
337	
338	A missing token is an escalation to the UI designer (§8), not a number you invent.
339	
340	If you must ship a placeholder pending sign-off, make it a **named constant with a comment
341	containing `provisional`, `pending`, or `placeholder`** — `npm run audit:tokens` reads that
342	comment and downgrades the finding to an acknowledged exception rather than a violation.
343	`audit-allow: <reason>` works too.
344	
345	Current state: **19 unacknowledged violations** repo-wide. Don't add to it.
346	
347	### Compound values and shorthand order
348	
349	```ts
350	padding: 'xs 0',        // ❌ emitted verbatim, browser drops it
351	paddingInline: 0,       // ✅
352	```
353	
354	Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value. And a shorthand declared *after* a
355	longhand resets it — `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock` wipes it.
356	
357	### Figma comparison
358	
359	Text nodes report a **cap-height box** and are **not comparable** to a CSS line box. Frames and
360	instances report a **real box** and are. A uniform residual across siblings is measurement; a
361	varying one is a defect. Full method in `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §5.
362

369	Registry, then `ui-kits/`, then the base package.

372	
373	**Use as-is** → done.
374	
375	**Override** → copy-first (§2). Keep the kebab-case filename. If the component is used
376	internally by SFCC's own components, the **default export must stay a faithful port** — full
377	prop surface, same `forwardRef` — with Zimmermann styling behind a named export. Check with:

385	(`'../swatch-group'`), not the base path. The resolver is webpack-only — Storybook and Vitest

405	## 5. Storybook — non-negotiable, and your build surface
406	
407	Every component exported from its folder needs `index.stories.tsx`. Build *in* Storybook, not
408	in the running app.
409	
410	### Categorisation
411	
412	`Foundation/` · `Elements/` · `Layout/` · `Commerce/` · `Forms/` · `Pages/` · `Contentful/`
413	
414	⚠️ **Story `title` is a different axis from the folder.** Folder = composition depth;
415	`title` = domain. `zimmModal` is an atom that lives under `Elements/`;
416	`zimmSubscribeSection` is an organism under `Forms/`.
417	
418	### Content
419	
420	Every file has a `Default`. Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`),
421	not every prop combination. Add `play` only where there's interactive behaviour worth
422	asserting.
423	
424	```tsx
425	import {expect, userEvent, within} from 'storybook/test'
426	```
427	
428	⚠️ **`@storybook/test` is not installed.** `.claude/rules/testing.md:115` prescribes it;
429	Storybook 10 moved it to `storybook/test`. Following that line verbatim breaks. The rule is
430	wrong, not your code.
431	
432	### Two things Storybook won't show truthfully
433	
434	- **Base-template SVGs render as empty boxes.** `.storybook/main.js` `ignore-loader`s them,
435	  mirroring the browser build — so an icon sourced from `@salesforce/retail-react-app` shows
436	  blank in Storybook while rendering correctly in the app. Our own icons in `zimm.tsx` are
437	  unaffected. **A blank icon in Storybook is usually a sourcing signal, not a broken glyph.**
438	- **`test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.** Running it against the dev server makes
439	  results uninterpretable.
440	- **Portalled content is not inside `canvasElement`.** `canvasElement` is `#storybook-root`, a
441	  *sibling* of the portal target. Measured: 0 dialogs inside the canvas against 1 in the
442	  document. Query `document` for a portalled dialog and use `findByRole`, not `getByRole` —
443	  the render promise resolves from `useLayoutEffect`, before passive effects have mounted the
444	  portal. `testing.md:128`'s "never reach into `document`" has no portal carve-out; that's a
445	  documentation gap.
446	
447	### The commands
448	
449	```bash
450	npm run storybook                                # the build surface
451	npm run build-storybook && npx test-storybook    # interaction + a11y — needs a BUILT storybook
452	```
453	
454	Interaction tests catch things the other layers can't: on the footer PR, making a text-input
455	control opt-in removed a button a `play` function clicked. `tsc`, `lint` and `vitest` were all
456	green; CI caught it at **1 failure in 73**.
457	
458	### Your branch gets a live MRT URL automatically
459	
460	`deploy-preview.yml` deploys every push to `feature/**`/`fix/**` to its own ephemeral MRT
461	environment and posts the URL. Use it for the three-surface review in §9.
462	
463	- **One environment per branch, not per commit** — reused on later pushes, and the comment
464	  updates in place.
465	- **Torn down automatically** when the PR closes or the branch is deleted.
466	- A real Sydney-hosted (`ap-southeast-2`) storefront with real dev environment variables — not
467	  a mock.
468	- **Excluded:** `fix/release-*` and `hotfix/*`.
469	- **No URL?** The branch had no open PR when it was pushed. Push again once the PR exists.

473	## 6. Accessibility — written as AC, not added later
474	
475	WCAG **2.2** AA. Fall back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible, and document why.
476	
477	Standing AC set for every component:
478	
479	- Keyboard operable, in a sensible order
480	- Visible focus indicator
481	- Accessible name on every control
482	- Correct semantic element (`button` for actions, `a` for navigation)
483	- Colour contrast 4.5:1 body / 3:1 large
484	- **24×24 minimum target size** (2.5.8 — a 2.2 addition, easy to miss from a 2.1 checklist)
485	
486	### [CORRECTED] a11y IS gated in CI
487	
488	An earlier revision of this manual, and two separate analyses since, concluded a11y is ungated
489	because there is no `.storybook/test-runner.js`. **That is Storybook 8 knowledge and is wrong
490	for what's installed.** `@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`'s `setup-page-script.js:390-397` reads
491	`story.parameters?.a11y?.test` and throws when it's `"error"`; `.storybook/preview.tsx:44` sets
492	exactly that.
493	
494	**Do not delete that `preview.tsx` block.** Honest rider: the gate has never been made to fail
495	on purpose, so it is *unproven*, not absent.
496	
497	### The two security rules
498	
499	`semgrep.yml` holds the only *security* gates in the review layer, both `ERROR` severity:
500	`dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` and `payment-credential-logged`.
501	
502	Both have real blind spots, so don't read a clean run as clearance. The XSS rule only excludes
503	an **inline** `.sanitize()` — so the idiomatic `const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(dirty)` form is
504	flagged as an ERROR while a spread-props form evades it entirely. The credential rule's sinks
505	are only `console.*` and `Sentry.*`, missing `dataLayer.push`, `localStorage`, query strings and
506	response bodies — and its name list omits **`cvc`**.
507	
508	### What the ast-grep rules miss
509	
510	All three are `severity: warning`.
511	
512	- `img-missing-alt` matches `^img$` only — **Chakra's `<Image>` is invisible to it.**
513	- The `IconButton` rule's `^aria-label\b` **does not match `aria-labelledby`** — the more
514	  correct answer gets flagged.
515	- The clickable-non-interactive rule checks neither `tabIndex` nor `onKeyDown`, despite
516	  `components.md` requiring both.
517	
518	Get these right at authoring time; don't rely on the tooling.

522	## 7. Data availability per tier
523	
524	**Your component is not done until its data exists where it ships.**
525	
526	This is new, and it's here because the footer passed every gate, rendered perfectly in dev and
527	Storybook, and was **blank on the test tier**. Nothing in the component was wrong.
528	
529	### The two mechanisms are separate
530	
531	| | Content **types** (schema) | Content (**entries**) |
532	|---|---|---|
533	| Deploy | `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` | *nothing automated* |
534	
535	**An Environment Template cannot carry entries.** It's structural — the SDK type has slots for
536	`contentTypeTemplates` and `editorInterfaceTemplates` and nothing else. The only entry-writing
537	code in the repo seeds the 11 `region` entries.
538	
539	### Verified state, 2026-08-25
540	
541	| tier | types | entries |
542	|---|---|---|
543	| **dev** | 14 | 42 |
544	| test / sit / uat / staging | **0** | **0** |
545	
546	The environments exist and are empty. Nothing has ever been promoted out of dev. **The
547	template covers only 5 of dev's 14 types** — the other 9 were UI-authored and have no code
548	representation.
549	
550	### Before you say a component works on a tier
551	
552	```bash
553	curl -s "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/<space>/environments/<env>/entries?content_type=<type>&limit=1" \
554	  -H "Authorization: Bearer <that tier's delivery token>"
555	```
556	
557	`total: 1` → it will render. `unknownContentType` → the model was never installed. Use
558	`limit=1`; the CDA returns an unreliable `total` at `limit=0`.
559	
560	### Fetch depth is load-bearing
561	
562	The footer passes `include: 3` (`footer/index.tsx:27`) where the shared `useContentful.ts`
563	hardcodes `include=2`. That is not arbitrary. At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved stubs, a
564	field access throws, the `.catch` swallows it, and the **entire component renders nothing**.
565	A depth mistake is indistinguishable from a network failure when you're looking at the page.
566	
567	**Check the Network tab before assuming the component is broken.** Eight distinct failure modes
568	look identical from the rendered page.

589	## 9. Before you open a PR
590	
591	### Gate zero — does it build
592	
593	```bash
594	npx tsc --noEmit
595	npm run lint
596	npm run test
597	npm run audit:tokens
598	npm run build
599	```
600	
601	⚠️ **Vitest does not run `play` functions.** Storybook interaction tests are a separate
602	command against a *built* Storybook.
603	
604	⚠️ **`lint`, `tsc` and `audit:tokens` are gated nowhere in CI.** If you don't run them, nobody
605	does. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide on pre-existing prettier errors.
606	
607	### Two repo-specific failure modes
608	
609	- **A `develop` merge can delete a declaration your branch depends on.** Re-run `tsc` **after**
610	  every merge, not just before.
611	- **The rule can be wrong, not your code.** Several `.claude/rules/` lines currently prescribe
612	  things that break — `testing.md:87`'s `@storybook/test`, `testing.md:100`'s missing portal
613	  carve-out. Check the rule against the installed package before contorting the code.
614	
615	### Three-surface self-review
616	
617	Review your own PR the way the reviewer will:
618	
619	1. **The diff** — token usage, naming, dead code, test coverage.
620	2. **The preview environment** — the MRT URL on your branch.
621	3. **Figma, side by side** — at mobile *and* desktop. Layout bugs are invisible in a diff and
622	   invisible to every automated gate.
623	
624	### Local CodeRabbit
625	
626	```bash
627	coderabbit auth status
628	cr review --light --base develop
629	```
630	
631	Required by AGENTS.md, verified by nothing. Use judgement on whether a flagged finding is worth
632	fixing now or leaving for the PR review — but the review must actually run.
633	
634	### Self-check
635	
636	- [ ] `tsc`, `lint`, `test`, `audit:tokens`, `build` all clean
637	- [ ] Story exists, with `play` if there's interactive behaviour
638	- [ ] Test exists if there's branching or event wiring
639	- [ ] No raw hex/px/rem/em without a `provisional`/`pending`/`audit-allow` comment
640	- [ ] No bare token key on a sizing or typography prop
641	- [ ] Recipe namespaced and registered in `theme/components/index.ts`
642	- [ ] Keyboard-operable, focus visible, names on all controls, 24×24 targets
643	- [ ] Compared against Figma at mobile and desktop
644	- [ ] Jira URL in the PR body (the Forge app isn't installed — nothing does this for you)
645	- [ ] Protection-tier block filled honestly
646	- [ ] Australian spelling in Zimmermann-authored identifiers and copy (`colour`, `centre`)
647	- [ ] No magic numbers or strings — named constant or config module
648	- [ ] JSDoc on anything with ≥2 callers, every exported hook, any non-obvious utility
649	- [ ] Minimal change — no base functionality removed or replaced unless asked
650	- [ ] Existing comments and commented-out code left alone
651	- [ ] `console.log` copy-first markers removed; no stray `console.*`
652	- [ ] Only one protection tier touched
653	- [ ] No `Co-Authored-By` trailer
654	
655	### ⚠️ Read the check *history*, not the head SHA
656	
657	**A skipped required check counts as passing.** `detect-changes` diffs
658	`since_last_remote_commit`, so a final docs-only commit can flip both required checks to green
659	even if an earlier push failed them. This happened on PR #59 — a 93-commit PR became
660	merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**.
661	
662	Read `gh pr checks` for `skipping`, not just for green.

666	## 10. Responding to a CodeRabbit review
667	
668	**Reply in-thread to every finding — fixed or not.** CodeRabbit's learning picks up patterns
669	from PR conversation. Silence teaches it nothing; a fix commit with no reply doesn't count.
670	
671	- **Fixed** → a short reply confirming it, referencing the commit.
672	- **Not fixing** → explain *which specific rule or doc* justifies it, so the same pattern gets
673	  recognised next time instead of re-flagged.
674	
675	Nothing enforces this: `requiresConversationResolution` is `false` on all three protected
676	branches, so a PR merges with every thread unanswered.
677	
678	### What the declines on PR #59 established
679	
680	These encode more project convention than the fixes did:
681	
682	- **Only four files are true absolutes** — `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`,
683	  `worker/main.js`. Being Tier 1 is not by itself disqualifying; being one of the four named
684	  absolutes is.
685	- **Never argue "the rationale isn't engaged"** against unconditionally-worded text. That's an
686	  over-read, and it was conceded as one.
687	- **An incidental Tier 1 edit that *could* be split out *should* be.** Declining on mootness is
688	  the weak position.
689	- **Fixing a bug in one component doesn't license touching its neighbours** (Hard Rule #5) —
690	  even a confirmed real bug, if it's pre-existing and out of scope. The systemic fix is a lint
691	  rule with its own story.
692	- **Never accept CodeRabbit's offer to open a GitHub issue.** This project tracks in Jira; a
693	  GitHub issue is a parallel tracker nobody watches.
694	- **When a repo rule is stated unconditionally, conform even for a provable no-op** — and add
695	  an inline comment saying so, so the next reader doesn't hunt for phantom state.
696	- **Cite the PRD line before you cite it.** A wrong citation in a decline poisons CodeRabbit's
697	  learning store and has to be retracted in-thread, not silently amended in a later commit.
698	
699	### Two switches that silence it invisibly
700	
701	`chore(deps)` or `dependabot` **in the PR title** disables CodeRabbit entirely — title-matched,
702	not author-matched. So does draft status. Neither shows as a failing check; it just goes quiet.
703	
704	---
705	
706	## 11. Hard stops
707	
708	1. Never work on `develop` or `main`.
709	2. Never modify a Tier 1 file without it being named in the prompt and owner approval confirmed.
710	3. Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`.
711	4. Never modify `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` — absolute,
712	   no exception.
713	5. Never refactor upward. Fixing a component doesn't mean touching the hook it calls.
714	6. Never rename or move a shared hook or component.
715	7. Never add or remove packages without Integration approval. When approved, `npm install` —
716	   don't hand-edit `package.json`.
717	8. Never modify test configuration.
718	9. Never delete files without being explicitly asked.
719	10. Never touch more than one protection tier in a change without confirming scope.
720	11. Never commit, push, or open a PR without an explicit request in the current prompt.
721	    Resuming from a summary or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit.
722	
723	### Shared shell needs coordination
724	
725	`header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/`, `seo/`, `_app/`, `_app-config/`,
726	`uiCopyProvider/`, `routes.tsx` are Tier 2 Global Shell, owned by **both** squads. Coordinate
727	before touching.
728	
729	⚠️ **`.claude/rules/` is documentation; `CODEOWNERS` is configuration.** When you want to know
730	what will actually block a merge, read `CODEOWNERS`. It has **no catch-all rule**, so a path
731	absent from it needs no code-owner review regardless of what any rules file says. `squadA.md`
732	and `squadB.md` are six weeks stale and contradict `CODEOWNERS` on PDP ownership — CODEOWNERS
733	says Squad B and is the one that enforces.
734	
735	---
736	
737	## 12. Performance
738	
739	LCP ≤ **2s at p75 mobile**. Not a polish pass.
740	
741	- **Images** — always lazy-load, always serve correctly sized. Never render a full-resolution
742	  image at thumbnail size.
743	- **Code splitting** — dynamic `import()` for anything heavy not needed on first render.
744	- **Data fetching** — request only the fields you need; parallelise. Waterfalls are not
745	  acceptable.
746	- **Third-party** — nothing loads before consent, and nothing consent-gated may block LCP. Use
747	  `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection.
748	- **Bundle** — `main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB, enforced by `bundlesize2`.
749	
750	⚠️ **No CSS budget exists.** `projectState.md`'s "main.css < 50 kB" was never implemented. CSS
751	growth is currently ungated in both directions.
752	
753	---
754	
755	## 13. Quick reference
756	
757	```bash
758	/session-start                   # branch check + tracking docs + health check
759	/scope-check                     # is this in this sprint, and whose territory?
760	/code-quality                    # read-only audit of the branch diff
761	/pr-checklist                    # pre-PR sweep
762	```
763	
764	```bash
765	npx tsc --noEmit                 # gated nowhere — run it yourself
766	npm run lint                     # gated nowhere
767	npm run test                     # Vitest — required check on develop
768	npm run audit:tokens             # gated nowhere; 19 violations outstanding
769	npm run build
770	cr review --light --base develop
771	```
772	
773	`npm start` — **do not run.** Ask for a restart if needed.
774	
775	| What | Where |
776	|---|---|
777	| Design tokens (Tier 1) | `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` |
778	| Registered recipes | `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` |
779	| Co-located recipe | `<component>/<name>.css.ts` |
780	| Zimmermann components | `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/` |
781	| Icons — **single source of truth** | `overrides/app/components/icons` |
782	| Shared types | `overrides/app/types/` |
783	
784	**Icons:** never import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`. If an icon is
785	missing from the overrides set, ask — don't substitute a visually similar one.
786	(`header/index.tsx:60` currently violates this.)
787	
788	### The eight things people get wrong most
789	
790	1. A bare token key on a **sizing** prop — `width: 'xl'` = 576px.
791	2. A recipe not namespaced, silently merging into a base SFCC recipe.
792	3. A recipe not registered — runtime throw on destructuring.
793	4. A base-path import of an already-overridden component — renders the base version in
794	   Storybook and Vitest.
795	5. `padding: 'xs 0'` — compound values never tokenise.
796	6. A raw literal with no `provisional`/`pending` comment.
797	7. Assuming the component is broken when the **data doesn't exist on that tier**.
798	8. Reading a PR's head-SHA checks as green when they're actually `skipping`.
799	
800	---
801	
802	*Revised 25 August 2026 against `develop` @ `8362b3c` (PR #59 merged, 93 commits). Corrections
803	in this pass: the `var(--zimm-*)` hierarchy had inverted and this manual taught the old rule;
804	a11y **is** gated and this manual said it wasn't; `@storybook/test` is not installed;
805	`auditTokenUsage.mjs` now exists and reports 19 violations; the overridden-directory count is
806	eleven, not seven; `theme/components/button.ts` no longer exists. Section 7 (data availability
807	per tier) and section 10 (responding to CodeRabbit) are new.*
808
