# FED Build Manual — Manual UI Build & Delivery

**Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 · **Revised:** 25 August 2026

The developer-facing half. This is the sequenced procedure for taking a Zimmermann UI story
from session start to merged PR.

**Companions:** `uiBuild-knowledge.md` (why the machine behaves the way it does — read it when
something fails silently) · `fedLead-playbook.md` (the lead role: refinement, estimation,
review culture, escalation).

**Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`. If this manual and that file
disagree, **that file wins** — and tell me, because it means this one is stale.

---

## 1. The Operating Principles

### Static-first

Props in, markup out. A component under `overrides/app/components/` receives its data and
renders it. It does not fetch.

Mock data goes in the story — never a temporary fetch you intend to remove. A component that
owns its own data-fetching cannot be reused where the data arrives differently: SSR-prefetched,
mocked in Storybook, or composed by a parent that already has it.

**The one exception**, and it is narrow: Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks
(`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called from any component, including a presentational leaf.
They read from a Provider mounted above the route tree, so they don't create the
SSR/Storybook/composition problem the rule exists to prevent. This covers content identical for
every consumer regardless of route — not anything that varies per page.

⚠️ **Their no-Provider behaviour differs and it will bite you in tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades
to fallback text and renders with zero setup. **`useIntl` throws**, and its `IntlProvider` is
mounted by the base SFCC `_app`, not `_app-config` — a narrower subtree than you'd expect. Any
Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer must wrap it.

### Leverage what already exists

Four rungs, in order:

1. **Use the base SFCC component as-is.**
2. **Override it** — mirror the path under `overrides/`, keep the kebab-case filename.

**The default is override, not build — because an override inherits the wiring for free.**
Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the
add-to-cart modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. And because the
resolver rewires imports transparently, overriding a component that SFCC's own base components
import means **the entire base template inherits your version with zero call sites touched**.

Worked examples: size selector → `swatch-group`; add to bag → `product-view`; max quantity →
`quantity-picker`; variant resolution → `use-controlled-variations` / `use-derived-product`.
Check what the base already does before scoping — a ticket saying "Cart API integration is in
scope" may be describing a call the base already makes.
3. **Compose existing ui-kit atoms** into something new.
4. **Build a new component.** Rarest. Justify it.

Before rung 4, check the registry (`.claude/registry/`) and grep `ui-kits/`.

**What `shared/ui` is actually for:** Contentful renderers need *primitives*, not commerce
components. Every Contentful component on `develop` already pulls them in — `duplexSection`
(`Box`, `Text`), `collectionHero` (`Box`, `Button`, `Heading`, `Text`), `hotspotPopup`,
`imageText`, `heroBanner`. Upstream those resolve to bare Chakra.

⚠️ **But the barrel is not the leverage play it looks like.** Overriding
`shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate branded styling into base cart/checkout/account **does not
work** — `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite,
and 212 base files import the barrel (195 excluding tests) while **0** import the individual module. See
`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §4.

### Figma stays open the whole time

Not at the end. **And check the Jira card's Figma link actually points at your frame** — a
stale link propagates: you build the wrong thing, the BA signs off against a different frame,
QA tests a third source. If it's wrong, ask the BA to fix the card rather than working it out
in a DM.

There are **two Figma files** and cross-comparing them produces confident nonsense. See
`uiBuild-knowledge.md` §5.

### Ask in the group chat

Roughly 30 minutes stuck is the trigger. One question at a time.

### The bar you're building to

The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3** — the whole project, not per sprint. (Contract figure;
nothing in `.docs/` records it.) Expect UI PRs
to be reviewed against the preview environment **and** Figma. Self-review the same way before
you open it (§9) — it's faster than a review round-trip.

---

## 2. Before you write any code

### Confirm the branch

```bash
git branch --show-current
```

If it's `develop` or `main`, stop. No changes.

### Check what already exists

Read `.claude/registry/` for the component. The `Origin` column is what matters:

| Origin | Means |
|---|---|
| `Custom` | Zimmermann-authored, already here |
| `Override` | already mirrored into `overrides/` |
| **`Base`** | **still upstream — you pay copy-first** |

⚠️ **Do not trust the registry's `Tier` column.** `generateRegistry.mjs:125-203` hardcodes tier
arrays, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything else to Tier 4. Paths are reliable;
tiers are not. For what actually blocks, read `CODEOWNERS`.

### The three component families

| Family | Casing | Example |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | kebab-case, matching upstream exactly | `product-tile/` |
| **ui-kit component** | **camelCase — the default for new work** | `zimmButton/` |
| `shared/ui` primitive | PascalCase, mirroring upstream | `Button/` |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Naming a Zimmermann-
authored file in kebab-case falsely signals Salesforce origin — which inverts the convention's
whole purpose.

### Where a new component goes

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
  index.tsx
  index.stories.tsx
  <name>.css.ts          ← the recipe
  index.test.tsx         ← if it has branching or event wiring
```

**Tier by composition, read off the imports:**

- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit
- **molecule** — composes atoms, light local state
- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**

An icon passed as a prop doesn't count. Slotted children don't count.

### What's actually overridden today

Eleven directories:

```
_app-config  button  contentful  footer  foundation  header
icons  pageContainer  product-view  ui-kits  uiCopyProvider
```

Still base, despite being referenced throughout `.claude/rules/`: `product-tile`,
`display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu`, `seo`.
**Assume most stories pay copy-first.**

### The copy-first rule

For any task requiring an override that doesn't exist yet, prepare **all of them at once**
before any functional change:

1. Copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path.
2. Convert to `.ts`/`.tsx`, update imports.
3. `npx tsc --noEmit`.
4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` to each.
5. **Stop.** Let the user confirm the overrides are rendering.
6. Remove the `console.log`s, then make functional changes.

Never bundle this silently with functional work.

---

## 3. Design Foundations

*The longest section, and the part that moves. Read it before your first component.*

### The styling hierarchy

1. **`textStyle`** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`. All 22
   Handover text styles are registered:

   `heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong`
   `body2` · `mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg`
   `linkSm` · `button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif`
2. **`var(--zimm-*)`** for colour and spacing. The spacing scale:

   | | | | | | | |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | `3xs` 2px | `2xs` 4px | `xs` 8px | `s` 12px | `m` 16px | `l` 20px | `xl` 24px |
   | `2xl` 32px | `3xl` 40px | `4xl` 64px | `5xl` 80px | `6xl` 128px | `7xl` 160px | |

   Semantic colour groups in `foundation/colour.ts`: `background` (01–07), `text`, `border`,
   `status`, `link`, `icon`, `action` (`primary.*`, `secondary.*`).
3. **The component's own recipe** for anything varying by variant/size/state.
4. **`sx`** for a one-off prop-system gap.
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it. In practice: never. There is
   no `.scss` anywhere in the footer or `ui-kits`.

### ⚠️ [CORRECTED] Rung 2 inverted — bare token strings are now wrong

An earlier revision of this manual taught `color="text.default"` and `padding="m"`, and said
seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was a smell. **That is backwards from the current rule.**

```tsx
// ❌ bare Chakra/theme token string in an override component
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

⚠️ **Two different rules are in play and it's easy to conflate them.** A bare key on a *spacing*
prop is **correct but against house style** — `theme.space` is registered, so it resolves. A bare
key on a *sizing or typography* prop is **broken** — those scales aren't registered at all. The
first gets a review comment; the second ships a 576px icon.

The reason is **house style, not correctness** — a bare key resolves identically, but forces a
reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it's correct.

`textStyle` stays a bare key. It's the one exception: there's no `var()` for the composite.

**In practice this rarely arises**, because brand values mostly shouldn't be in JSX at all.
Measured on `develop`: `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **18 recipe files** and exactly **one**
component `.tsx` — a conditional `paddingLeft` no Chakra prop expresses. Type via `textStyle`,
colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine gap.

### Icon, action and motion values are constants, not theme tokens

They collide with Chakra's scales the same way — `theme.sizes.lg` is 32rem and backs `boxSize`
everywhere — so they are **imported directly** rather than registered:

```tsx
import { iconSizes, actionSizes, motion } from 'app/theme/foundation';

<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />            // 20px
<Button height={actionSizes.height.lg} />  // 52px
```

| | |
|---|---|
| `iconSizes` | `lg` 20px · `md` 16px · `sm` 12px |
| `actionSizes` | `height.{lg: 52, md: 40}` · `paddingX.{lg: 32, md: 20}` · `gap: 16` |
| `motion` | `duration.{fast: 200, default: 300, slow: 500}ms` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}` |

⚠️ **Motion values are PROVISIONAL**, pending designer sign-off — `motion.ts` says so itself.

`borderWidth.default` is 1px. `focusRingOffsets.default` is 2px, `.secondary` 3px — the second
exists to clear the secondary button's 1px border.

### ⚠️ The trap: a spacing key on a sizing prop

**This shipped a completely broken footer, so it's worth being blunt about.**

```tsx
padding: 'xl',   // ✅ reads theme.space.xl
width: 'xl',     // ❌ reads theme.sizes.xl = 36rem = 576px
```

Only `space` is registered. `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` are not.
Measured blow-up range **8×–112×**. And `s`/`m`/`l` are absent from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
declarations are **dropped silently**.

Nothing catches this. `'xl'` is a valid `SystemStyleObject` value so TypeScript is satisfied,
no lint rule exists, and no test asserts layout. It passed `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`,
CodeRabbit (local *and* PR) and the Storybook a11y run — only rendering the page found it.

`recipeGuards.test.ts` now guards it **inside recipes**. It cannot see a JSX prop.

### ⚠️ `extendTheme` MERGES — it does not replace

Name a recipe `Footer` and it deep-merges into base SFCC's `Footer`, inheriting parts you never
wrote. Namespace everything: `ZimmFooter`.

`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — those three are deliberate. Anything
else must be namespaced, and `recipeGuards.test.ts` fails the build if it isn't.

⚠️ A recipe unit test **cannot catch this**: `extendTheme` doesn't populate `theme.__cssMap`,
only `ChakraProvider` does. A direct `css()(theme)` assertion passes vacuously.

### Responsive steps are explicit media queries

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: {
  flexDirection: 'row',
  padding: `var(--zimm-scale-4xl) var(--zimm-scale-3xl) ${SPACE_SECTION}`,
},
```

Two reasons. The array shorthand (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) puts a bare token key at every
step and the guard flags all four. And `BP.desktop` (64em) **conflicts with Chakra's `lg`=62em
/ `xl`=80em**, so a responsive prop silently steps at the wrong width.

### Register the recipe or it throws

Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path.
Co-location is therefore free — but the key must be in `theme/components/index.ts` or
destructuring throws at runtime.

**A registered recipe nothing reads is dead code.** Chakra's `<Button>`/`<Link>` read theirs
automatically; a custom multipart component must call `useMultiStyleConfig` (or `useStyleConfig`
for a single-part one). A registered-but-unread recipe looks like compliance and changes nothing.

The consumption pattern is always three lines:

```ts
const ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooter';
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE, {});
```

### Interaction state belongs in CSS, not React state

`_hover`, `_active`, `_focusVisible`, `_disabled` in the recipe. Not `useState` + `onMouseEnter`.
It looks identical in a screenshot and behaves differently in five ways that all matter:
touch devices, keyboard focus, rapid pointer movement, SSR output, and re-render cost.

⚠️ A programmatic `.focus()` does **not** match `:focus-visible`. A ring styled only on
`:focus-visible` won't appear after a scripted focus move.

### `.zimm-*` global classes

~28 classes live in `globalStyles.ts` — `.zimm-text-*`, `.zimm-form-*`, `.zimm-grid`,
`.zimm-focus-visible`. They ship on **every page** and have almost no consumers today (one
Storybook demo uses `.zimm-grid`).

**There are no `.zimm-btn-*` classes, and there must never be.** A component with both a class
and a recipe has two surfaces that drift. Use Chakra's `<Button>`.

Don't reach for a class for new work — a registered recipe, always. The classes remain
defensible only for genuinely static, non-interactive, massively-reused treatments.

### You don't add tokens

A missing token is an escalation to the UI designer (§8), not a number you invent.

If you must ship a placeholder pending sign-off, make it a **named constant with a comment
containing `provisional`, `pending`, or `placeholder`** — `npm run audit:tokens` reads that
comment and downgrades the finding to an acknowledged exception rather than a violation.
`audit-allow: <reason>` works too.

Current state: **19 unacknowledged violations** repo-wide. Don't add to it.

### Compound values and shorthand order

```ts
padding: 'xs 0',        // ❌ emitted verbatim, browser drops it
paddingInline: 0,       // ✅
```

Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value. And a shorthand declared *after* a
longhand resets it — `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock` wipes it.

### Figma comparison

Text nodes report a **cap-height box** and are **not comparable** to a CSS line box. Frames and
instances report a **real box** and are. A uniform residual across siblings is measurement; a
varying one is a defect. Full method in `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §5.

---

## 4. The build sequence

### Step 1 — does it exist?

Registry, then `ui-kits/`, then the base package.

### Step 2 — pick the rung

**Use as-is** → done.

**Override** → copy-first (§2). Keep the kebab-case filename. If the component is used
internally by SFCC's own components, the **default export must stay a faithful port** — full
prop surface, same `forwardRef` — with Zimmermann styling behind a named export. Check with:

```bash
grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

⚠️ **When importing a component that already has an override, use a relative path**
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the base path. The resolver is webpack-only — Storybook and Vitest
don't load it, so a base-path import silently renders the **unstyled base component** in both.

**Build custom** → §2's folder layout.

### Step 3 — execute

Named export matching the folder. Props type named for the component, declared at the top of
the file. Move it to `types.ts` only when a sibling file consumes it.

**Split when:** the component function passes ~150 lines, or branching gets deep. **Extract to
a hook when:** there are ≥2 related `useState` that change together, or a `useEffect` has a
non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function.

### Step 4 — apply design styles

Recipe first. `sx` for genuine gaps. Never a raw literal.

---

## 5. Storybook — non-negotiable, and your build surface

Every component exported from its folder needs `index.stories.tsx`. Build *in* Storybook, not
in the running app.

### Categorisation

`Foundation/` · `Elements/` · `Layout/` · `Commerce/` · `Forms/` · `Pages/` · `Contentful/`

⚠️ **Story `title` is a different axis from the folder.** Folder = composition depth;
`title` = domain. `zimmModal` is an atom that lives under `Elements/`;
`zimmSubscribeSection` is an organism under `Forms/`.

### Content

Every file has a `Default`. Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`),
not every prop combination. Add `play` only where there's interactive behaviour worth
asserting.

```tsx
import {expect, userEvent, within} from 'storybook/test'
```

⚠️ **`@storybook/test` is not installed.** `.claude/rules/testing.md:115` prescribes it;
Storybook 10 moved it to `storybook/test`. Following that line verbatim breaks. The rule is
wrong, not your code.

### Two things Storybook won't show truthfully

- **Base-template SVGs render as empty boxes.** `.storybook/main.js` `ignore-loader`s them,
  mirroring the browser build — so an icon sourced from `@salesforce/retail-react-app` shows
  blank in Storybook while rendering correctly in the app. Our own icons in `zimm.tsx` are
  unaffected. **A blank icon in Storybook is usually a sourcing signal, not a broken glyph.**
- **`test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.** Running it against the dev server makes
  results uninterpretable.
- **Portalled content is not inside `canvasElement`.** `canvasElement` is `#storybook-root`, a
  *sibling* of the portal target. Measured: 0 dialogs inside the canvas against 1 in the
  document. Query `document` for a portalled dialog and use `findByRole`, not `getByRole` —
  the render promise resolves from `useLayoutEffect`, before passive effects have mounted the
  portal. `testing.md:128`'s "never reach into `document`" has no portal carve-out; that's a
  documentation gap.

### The commands

```bash
npm run storybook                                # the build surface
npm run build-storybook && npx test-storybook    # interaction + a11y — needs a BUILT storybook
```

Interaction tests catch things the other layers can't: on the footer PR, making a text-input
control opt-in removed a button a `play` function clicked. `tsc`, `lint` and `vitest` were all
green; CI caught it at **1 failure in 73**.

### Your branch gets a live MRT URL automatically

`deploy-preview.yml` deploys every push to `feature/**`/`fix/**` to its own ephemeral MRT
environment and posts the URL. Use it for the three-surface review in §9.

- **One environment per branch, not per commit** — reused on later pushes, and the comment
  updates in place.
- **Torn down automatically** when the PR closes or the branch is deleted.
- A real Sydney-hosted (`ap-southeast-2`) storefront with real dev environment variables — not
  a mock.
- **Excluded:** `fix/release-*` and `hotfix/*`.
- **No URL?** The branch had no open PR when it was pushed. Push again once the PR exists.

## 6. Accessibility — written as AC, not added later

WCAG **2.2** AA. Fall back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible, and document why.

Standing AC set for every component:

- Keyboard operable, in a sensible order
- Visible focus indicator
- Accessible name on every control
- Correct semantic element (`button` for actions, `a` for navigation)
- Colour contrast 4.5:1 body / 3:1 large
- **24×24 minimum target size** (2.5.8 — a 2.2 addition, easy to miss from a 2.1 checklist)

### [CORRECTED] a11y IS gated in CI

An earlier revision of this manual, and two separate analyses since, concluded a11y is ungated
because there is no `.storybook/test-runner.js`. **That is Storybook 8 knowledge and is wrong
for what's installed.** `@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`'s `setup-page-script.js:390-397` reads
`story.parameters?.a11y?.test` and throws when it's `"error"`; `.storybook/preview.tsx:44` sets
exactly that.

**Do not delete that `preview.tsx` block.** Honest rider: the gate has never been made to fail
on purpose, so it is *unproven*, not absent.

### The two security rules

`semgrep.yml` holds the only *security* gates in the review layer, both `ERROR` severity:
`dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` and `payment-credential-logged`.

Both have real blind spots, so don't read a clean run as clearance. The XSS rule only excludes
an **inline** `.sanitize()` — so the idiomatic `const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(dirty)` form is
flagged as an ERROR while a spread-props form evades it entirely. The credential rule's sinks
are only `console.*` and `Sentry.*`, missing `dataLayer.push`, `localStorage`, query strings and
response bodies — and its name list omits **`cvc`**.

### What the ast-grep rules miss

All three are `severity: warning`.

- `img-missing-alt` matches `^img$` only — **Chakra's `<Image>` is invisible to it.**
- The `IconButton` rule's `^aria-label\b` **does not match `aria-labelledby`** — the more
  correct answer gets flagged.
- The clickable-non-interactive rule checks neither `tabIndex` nor `onKeyDown`, despite
  `components.md` requiring both.

Get these right at authoring time; don't rely on the tooling.

---

## 7. Data availability per tier

**Your component is not done until its data exists where it ships.**

This is new, and it's here because the footer passed every gate, rendered perfectly in dev and
Storybook, and was **blank on the test tier**. Nothing in the component was wrong.

### The two mechanisms are separate

| | Content **types** (schema) | Content (**entries**) |
|---|---|---|
| Deploy | `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` | *nothing automated* |

**An Environment Template cannot carry entries.** It's structural — the SDK type has slots for
`contentTypeTemplates` and `editorInterfaceTemplates` and nothing else. The only entry-writing
code in the repo seeds the 11 `region` entries.

### Verified state, 2026-08-25

| tier | types | entries |
|---|---|---|
| **dev** | 14 | 42 |
| test / sit / uat / staging | **0** | **0** |

The environments exist and are empty. Nothing has ever been promoted out of dev. **The
template covers only 5 of dev's 14 types** — the other 9 were UI-authored and have no code
representation.

### Before you say a component works on a tier

```bash
curl -s "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/<space>/environments/<env>/entries?content_type=<type>&limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <that tier's delivery token>"
```

`total: 1` → it will render. `unknownContentType` → the model was never installed. Use
`limit=1`; the CDA returns an unreliable `total` at `limit=0`.

### Fetch depth is load-bearing

The footer passes `include: 3` (`footer/index.tsx:27`) where the shared `useContentful.ts`
hardcodes `include=2`. That is not arbitrary. At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved stubs, a
field access throws, the `.catch` swallows it, and the **entire component renders nothing**.
A depth mistake is indistinguishable from a network failure when you're looking at the page.

**Check the Network tab before assuming the component is broken.** Eight distinct failure modes
look identical from the rendered page.

## 8. When you find a gap

Raise it, don't invent an answer. **One question at a time.**

| Gap | Goes to |
|---|---|
| Missing design token / spec value | UI designer |
| Ambiguous or contradictory requirement | BA, citing the doc and section |
| Missing Figma frame or stale card link | BA |
| Shared hook signature change | team RFC — not a PR |
| New package dependency | Integration team |
| Tier 1 file needed | see `fedLead-playbook.md` — verified-session exception may apply |
| Content model / field change | Integration / SI |
| Anything spanning two protection tiers | stop, confirm scope |

## 9. Before you open a PR

### Gate zero — does it build

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npm run test
npm run audit:tokens
npm run build
```

⚠️ **Vitest does not run `play` functions.** Storybook interaction tests are a separate
command against a *built* Storybook.

⚠️ **`lint`, `tsc` and `audit:tokens` are gated nowhere in CI.** If you don't run them, nobody
does. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide on pre-existing prettier errors.

### Two repo-specific failure modes

- **A `develop` merge can delete a declaration your branch depends on.** Re-run `tsc` **after**
  every merge, not just before.
- **The rule can be wrong, not your code.** Several `.claude/rules/` lines currently prescribe
  things that break — `testing.md:87`'s `@storybook/test`, `testing.md:100`'s missing portal
  carve-out. Check the rule against the installed package before contorting the code.

### Three-surface self-review

Review your own PR the way the reviewer will:

1. **The diff** — token usage, naming, dead code, test coverage.
2. **The preview environment** — the MRT URL on your branch.
3. **Figma, side by side** — at mobile *and* desktop. Layout bugs are invisible in a diff and
   invisible to every automated gate.

### Local CodeRabbit

```bash
coderabbit auth status
cr review --light --base develop
```

Required by AGENTS.md, verified by nothing. Use judgement on whether a flagged finding is worth
fixing now or leaving for the PR review — but the review must actually run.

### Self-check

- [ ] `tsc`, `lint`, `test`, `audit:tokens`, `build` all clean
- [ ] Story exists, with `play` if there's interactive behaviour
- [ ] Test exists if there's branching or event wiring
- [ ] No raw hex/px/rem/em without a `provisional`/`pending`/`audit-allow` comment
- [ ] No bare token key on a sizing or typography prop
- [ ] Recipe namespaced and registered in `theme/components/index.ts`
- [ ] Keyboard-operable, focus visible, names on all controls, 24×24 targets
- [ ] Compared against Figma at mobile and desktop
- [ ] Jira URL in the PR body (the Forge app isn't installed — nothing does this for you)
- [ ] Protection-tier block filled honestly
- [ ] Australian spelling in Zimmermann-authored identifiers and copy (`colour`, `centre`)
- [ ] No magic numbers or strings — named constant or config module
- [ ] JSDoc on anything with ≥2 callers, every exported hook, any non-obvious utility
- [ ] Minimal change — no base functionality removed or replaced unless asked
- [ ] Existing comments and commented-out code left alone
- [ ] `console.log` copy-first markers removed; no stray `console.*`
- [ ] Only one protection tier touched
- [ ] No `Co-Authored-By` trailer

### ⚠️ Read the check *history*, not the head SHA

**A skipped required check counts as passing.** `detect-changes` diffs
`since_last_remote_commit`, so a final docs-only commit can flip both required checks to green
even if an earlier push failed them. This happened on PR #59 — a 93-commit PR became
merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**.

Read `gh pr checks` for `skipping`, not just for green.

---

## 10. Responding to a CodeRabbit review

**Reply in-thread to every finding — fixed or not.** CodeRabbit's learning picks up patterns
from PR conversation. Silence teaches it nothing; a fix commit with no reply doesn't count.

- **Fixed** → a short reply confirming it, referencing the commit.
- **Not fixing** → explain *which specific rule or doc* justifies it, so the same pattern gets
  recognised next time instead of re-flagged.

Nothing enforces this: `requiresConversationResolution` is `false` on all three protected
branches, so a PR merges with every thread unanswered.

### What the declines on PR #59 established

These encode more project convention than the fixes did:

- **Only four files are true absolutes** — `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`,
  `worker/main.js`. Being Tier 1 is not by itself disqualifying; being one of the four named
  absolutes is.
- **Never argue "the rationale isn't engaged"** against unconditionally-worded text. That's an
  over-read, and it was conceded as one.
- **An incidental Tier 1 edit that *could* be split out *should* be.** Declining on mootness is
  the weak position.
- **Fixing a bug in one component doesn't license touching its neighbours** (Hard Rule #5) —
  even a confirmed real bug, if it's pre-existing and out of scope. The systemic fix is a lint
  rule with its own story.
- **Never accept CodeRabbit's offer to open a GitHub issue.** This project tracks in Jira; a
  GitHub issue is a parallel tracker nobody watches.
- **When a repo rule is stated unconditionally, conform even for a provable no-op** — and add
  an inline comment saying so, so the next reader doesn't hunt for phantom state.
- **Cite the PRD line before you cite it.** A wrong citation in a decline poisons CodeRabbit's
  learning store and has to be retracted in-thread, not silently amended in a later commit.

### Two switches that silence it invisibly

`chore(deps)` or `dependabot` **in the PR title** disables CodeRabbit entirely — title-matched,
not author-matched. So does draft status. Neither shows as a failing check; it just goes quiet.

## 11. Hard stops

1. Never work on `develop` or `main`.
2. Never modify a Tier 1 file without it being named in the prompt and owner approval confirmed.
3. Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`.
4. Never modify `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js` — absolute,
   no exception.
5. Never refactor upward. Fixing a component doesn't mean touching the hook it calls.
6. Never rename or move a shared hook or component.
7. Never add or remove packages without Integration approval. When approved, `npm install` —
   don't hand-edit `package.json`.
8. Never modify test configuration.
9. Never delete files without being explicitly asked.
10. Never touch more than one protection tier in a change without confirming scope.
11. Never commit, push, or open a PR without an explicit request in the current prompt.
    Resuming from a summary or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit.

### Shared shell needs coordination

`header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/`, `seo/`, `_app/`, `_app-config/`,
`uiCopyProvider/`, `routes.tsx` are Tier 2 Global Shell, owned by **both** squads. Coordinate
before touching.

⚠️ **`.claude/rules/` is documentation; `CODEOWNERS` is configuration.** When you want to know
what will actually block a merge, read `CODEOWNERS`. It has **no catch-all rule**, so a path
absent from it needs no code-owner review regardless of what any rules file says. `squadA.md`
and `squadB.md` are six weeks stale and contradict `CODEOWNERS` on PDP ownership — CODEOWNERS
says Squad B and is the one that enforces.

---

## 12. Performance

LCP ≤ **2s at p75 mobile**. Not a polish pass.

- **Images** — always lazy-load, always serve correctly sized. Never render a full-resolution
  image at thumbnail size.
- **Code splitting** — dynamic `import()` for anything heavy not needed on first render.
- **Data fetching** — request only the fields you need; parallelise. Waterfalls are not
  acceptable.
- **Third-party** — nothing loads before consent, and nothing consent-gated may block LCP. Use
  `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection.
- **Bundle** — `main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB, enforced by `bundlesize2`.

⚠️ **No CSS budget exists.** `projectState.md`'s "main.css < 50 kB" was never implemented. CSS
growth is currently ungated in both directions.

---

## 13. Quick reference

```bash
/session-start                   # branch check + tracking docs + health check
/scope-check                     # is this in this sprint, and whose territory?
/code-quality                    # read-only audit of the branch diff
/pr-checklist                    # pre-PR sweep
```

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit                 # gated nowhere — run it yourself
npm run lint                     # gated nowhere
npm run test                     # Vitest — required check on develop
npm run audit:tokens             # gated nowhere; 19 violations outstanding
npm run build
cr review --light --base develop
```

`npm start` — **do not run.** Ask for a restart if needed.

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Design tokens (Tier 1) | `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` |
| Registered recipes | `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` |
| Co-located recipe | `<component>/<name>.css.ts` |
| Zimmermann components | `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/` |
| Icons — **single source of truth** | `overrides/app/components/icons` |
| Shared types | `overrides/app/types/` |

**Icons:** never import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`. If an icon is
missing from the overrides set, ask — don't substitute a visually similar one.
(`header/index.tsx:60` currently violates this.)

### The eight things people get wrong most

1. A bare token key on a **sizing** prop — `width: 'xl'` = 576px.
2. A recipe not namespaced, silently merging into a base SFCC recipe.
3. A recipe not registered — runtime throw on destructuring.
4. A base-path import of an already-overridden component — renders the base version in
   Storybook and Vitest.
5. `padding: 'xs 0'` — compound values never tokenise.
6. A raw literal with no `provisional`/`pending` comment.
7. Assuming the component is broken when the **data doesn't exist on that tier**.
8. Reading a PR's head-SHA checks as green when they're actually `skipping`.

You own the template, 286 the BA fills it, you sign off the field IDs. 287 288 | Field ID | Type | Required | Localised | Notes | 289 |---|---|---|---|---| 290 | `image` | Media | yes | no | | 291 | `imageAlt` | Short text | yes | yes | empty string permitted for decorative | 292 | `bodyCopy` | Rich text | no | yes | absent case must render perceivably | 293 | `ctaLabel` | Short text | no | yes | required if `ctaUrl` set | 294 | `ctaUrl` | Short text | no | no | passes `isSafeHref`; external links get the 3.2.5 suffix | 295 296 **Field IDs, not display names.** "Body copy" in prose is where drift starts. The IDs are the 297 contract — a rename after authoring begins is a migration, not an edit. Requirement source is 298 `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §2. 299 300 ⚠️ **Studio Experiences inverts the order** — the contract is generated from the React props 301 rather than authored first, so the review point moves to the component's prop type. 302 303 --- 304 305 ## Play 5 — PR review 306 307 ### Already mechanical — don't spend review time here 308 309 Conventional commit format · registry regeneration · derived-config edit blocking · 310 `.env.sample` secret shapes · tag naming · the two `semgrep.yml` security rules (unsanitised 311 `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, payment-credential logging) · the three ast-grep a11y rules 312 (`warning` only) · Storybook a11y (`preview.tsx` sets 313 `a11y.test: 'error'`; the installed test-runner enforces it). 314 315 ⚠️ By Play 5b's own standard the a11y gate is **unproven** — it has never been made to fail on 316 purpose. It's on this list because it runs, not because it's been demonstrated to catch 317 anything. Worth one deliberate break to find out. 318 319 ### Gate zero — does it build 320 321 ⚠️ **Read the check *history*, not the head SHA.** `detect-changes` diffs 322 `since_last_remote_commit`, so a docs-only final commit flips both required checks green even 323 if an earlier push failed them. **A skipped required check counts as passing.** PR #59 merged 324 with all four suites `skipping` and zero test evidence on its head SHA. 325 326 Also: `Playwright E2E (localhost)` and `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)` are **required nowhere** — they can be red and 327 the PR merges. 328 329 ### Review across three surfaces 330 331 1. **The diff** — tokens, naming, dead code, test coverage. 332 2. **The preview environment** — every `feature/**`/`fix/**` push (except `fix/release-*`) gets its own MRT URL. 333 3. **Figma, side by side**, mobile *and* desktop. 334 335 Layout defects are invisible in a diff and invisible to every automated gate. `width: 'xl'` 336 resolving to 576px destroyed the footer on every page while passing `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, 337 CodeRabbit twice, and the a11y run. 338 339 ### The token checklist 340 341 - Bare token key on a **sizing** or **typography** prop → wrong or dropped silently 342 - Bare token string where `var(--zimm-*)` is now required 343 - Raw hex/px/rem/em without a `provisional`/`pending`/`audit-allow` comment 344 - Recipe not namespaced → silent deep-merge into a base SFCC recipe 345 - Recipe not registered → runtime throw 346 - Compound value (`padding: 'xs 0'`) → emitted verbatim, dropped 347 348 ### Tests and stories — the minimum 349 350 A story for anything exported. A test where there's branching or event wiring. Resolve 351 duplicate coverage by **scoping what the test asserts** — mock the child whose internals are 352 proven elsewhere — not by leaving the component with no test of its own. 353 354 ### Ten questions, in order 355 356 1. Does it build, and did the checks actually *run*? 357 2. Does it match Figma at both breakpoints? 358 3. Is anything here already in `ui-kits`? 359 4. Any raw design value? 360 5. Any bare token key on a sizing/typography prop? 361 6. Is the recipe namespaced and registered? 362 7. Keyboard operable, focus visible, names on controls, 24×24 targets? 363 8. Does the absent-data case render something perceivable? 364 9. Does its data exist on the tiers it must demo on? 365 10. Does the protection-tier block in the PR body match the actual diff? 366 367 --- 368 369 ## Play 5b — Verifying a claim before you act on it 370 371 *Learned expensively. Reversals here would each have shipped a wrong change.* 372 373 - **Absence in an extracted spec is not a decision.** A field missing from a Figma export may 374 mean "not specified" or "deliberately none" — those are different, and you can't tell from 375 the absence. 376 - **A codebase value isn't a spec until you find its source.** Someone typed it. Find out who 377 and why before treating it as intent. 378 - **Ask for the node.** A Figma *screenshot* in a ticket is not the frame. Node type decides 379 whether a measurement is even comparable. 380 - **Value-matching audits produce confident nonsense.** "These 41 literals should be tokens" 381 inflated from 19 by matching `.rem` inside `removeEventListener`. 382 - **A grep count is not a coverage verdict.** When a count returns zero, establish *which* 383 zero: untested, tested elsewhere, or unused. 384 - **A passing test can encode the bug.** A tie-break suite named "order doesn't change the 385 outcome" used only distinct timestamps — the one arrangement already order-independent. It 386 passed while the bug was live. 387 388 **The shape all of these share: a proxy reported as the finding.** 389 390 The standard: **make the check fail on purpose before its pass counts.** If something is 391 asserted rather than proven, say so. 392 393 --- 394 395 ## Play 6 — Accessibility 396 397 WCAG **2.2** AA. Per-component AC: keyboard operable · visible focus · accessible name · 398 correct semantic element · contrast 4.5:1 / 3:1 · **24×24 target size** (2.5.8, a 2.2 addition). 399 400 **What the tooling misses**, so don't treat a clean run as clearance: the `` ast-grep rule 401 matches `^img$` only and is blind to Chakra's ``; the `IconButton` rule rejects 402 `aria-labelledby` — the more correct answer — because of a word-boundary bug; the 403 clickable-non-interactive rule checks neither `tabIndex` nor `onKeyDown`. All three are 404 `severity: warning`. 405 406 **Open item:** whether missing alt text should be absent or `alt=""` is a content-model 407 question, not a code one. Needs a decision from Tim. 408 409 --- 410 411 ## Play 7 — Page-level validation 412 413 | Part | Where it lands today | 414 |---|---| 415 | E2E | partial — **one spec file exists in the entire repo** | 416 | Lighthouse | yes, at SIT tier | 417 | **Design parity** | **no automated home — defaults to you** | 418 419 ⚠️ **No page has a Storybook story**, despite `components.md` requiring one for page-level 420 assemblies. 421 422 The `@area` vocabulary is `homepage · checkout · search · account · pdp · plp · integrations`. 423 Only `homepage` has a spec, and only `e2e_homepage` is mapped in the change-scoping config — 424 each new area's first spec needs its own allow-list group or it silently falls back to the full 425 suite. 426 427 Visual regression (Chromatic / Loki / Percy) would give design parity an automated home. It's a 428 new dependency and a budget line, so it needs approval before it's proposed as a plan. 429 430 --- 431 432 ## Play 8 — Pushing back before sizing 433 434 **The Figma link on the card is a build input.** A stale link propagates three ways: the dev 435 builds the wrong thing, the BA signs off against a different frame, QA tests a third source. 436 Ask the BA to fix the card. 437 438 **Decisions need a findable home.** A decision recorded only in a Teams thread will be 439 re-litigated within a month. 440 441 ### The product-side register — live, decision-blocking 442 443 | Open item | Position to hold | 444 |---|---| 445 | **Recommendations** | `SFCC-7` already holds eight decomposed tickets, and **SFCC-647 is `Ready for Development`** and answers the data-source question. Raise 647 — don't create tickets. | 446 | **Shop the Look naming** | Four names for possibly two things: "Shop the Look" (SFCC-90), "Shop the Edit" (SFCC-313), "Product Cards with Lookbook" (04.7), and `shoppableImage`, which already exists in code. Force one name before either is estimated. | 447 | **Preview & publishing** | The preview token is set on dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging/prod. Both preview paths 404 without it and are `noindex`. **Authors preview on `uat`.** "Can we preview on prod?" needs a Tier 1 change against a documented security rationale. | 448 | **Contentful pattern per component** | Entry-driven vs Studio Experiences. **Highest-value item to close** — it decides story order and whether the incremental-assembly loop is even available. | 449 | **`regions` content-model field** | Unconfirmed, and it affects every Contentful component's variant model across eight storefronts. | 450 | **Composed-page ownership** | "Not product/category → Contentful" doesn't settle PDP/PLP editorial blocks or category landing pages. **Category landing pages are the sharp edge, and PLP work is already in flight.** | 451 452 --- 453 454 ## Play 9 — Design-system escalation 455 456 Standing route for missing tokens: the weekly design review. 457 458 Live gaps: 459 460 - **Button has no Colour axis.** The 04.7 spec says "Normal, Inverse"; the implementation 461 exposes only `variant` + `size`. The registry reports **10 consumers**, so adding the axis 462 later touches ten call sites. 463 - **Icon Button is marked Done in 04.7 and has no implementation at all.** 464 - `zimmButton`'s provisional heights (50px/41px) disagree with Handover's `actionSizes` 465 (52px/40px); `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no token at all. 466 - **`textStyles.navigation`** is the only one of 22 hardcoding `lineHeight: 'normal'`; Figma 467 reportedly specifies 100%. 468 - **Spacing gaps** — 28px and 44px are in use with no named entry between `xl` (24) and `2xl` 469 (32), or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64). 470 - Primary-button hover fails AA at **2.96:1**; there's no inverse focus-ring token. 471 472 ⚠️ **"Done" in the 04.7 component tracker means design-confirmed, not API-matched.** Those are 473 different states and the tracker doesn't distinguish them. 474 475 **What to do when the design system itself is wrong** — e.g. a token that fails the project's 476 own WCAG 2.2 AA target — is unresolved. Someone has to accept that risk explicitly; right now 477 nobody has. 478 479 --- 480 481 ## Governance — what actually blocks 482 483 *Expanded. The short version: `.claude/rules/` is documentation, `CODEOWNERS` is 484 configuration.* 485 486 ### The real enforcement 487 488 Server-side and it works: `require_code_owner_reviews` + `enforce_admins` + 489 `bypass_pull_request_allowances: []` on `develop`, `main` and `release/**`. All five CODEOWNERS 490 teams exist and have members. 491 492 Advisory only: `tier1-guard`, `tier2-warning`, `cross-squad-guard`, and any assistant's 493 confirmation prompt. `tier1-guard` is deliberately not a required check — GitHub's Feb-2025 494 cross-run check-run lockdown made "hard-fail until approved" unimplementable. 495 496 ### Where the docs and the configuration disagree 497 498 | Path | Declared | CODEOWNERS | CI guard | 499 |---|---|---|---| 500 | `babel.config.js` | **Tier 1** | **absent** | **absent** | 501 | `tsconfig.json` | **Tier 1** | **absent** | **absent** | 502 | `theme/globalStyles.ts` | **Tier 2** | **absent** | **absent** | 503 | `overrides/app/ssr/**` | Tier 1 | ✓ | absent — the glob is `ssr.*`, a literal dot | 504 505 **`CODEOWNERS` has no catch-all rule.** A path absent from it requires zero code-owner review 506 regardless of what any rules file says. So editing `tsconfig.json` — strict mode and every path 507 alias — currently needs approval from nobody. 508 509 Also ungated: `scripts/versionGuard.mjs` (the entire downgrade-protection mechanism), 510 `.husky/*` (the shims that invoke the gated hooks — empty one and the gate is off). 511 512 ### Last-match-wins 513 514 `CODEOWNERS:186` (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only) is placed last among 515 the `components/` rules, deliberately downgrading any co-located recipe inside a Tier 2 516 directory. Rationale: a co-located recipe composes established tokens; authoring a new token 517 still means `theme/foundation/`. 518 519 ⚠️ It also means a `.css.ts` inside `_app-config/` or `seo/` would drop the Tier 2 gate the 520 same way. Nothing prevents that. 521 522 ### Squad ownership is stale 523 524 `squadA.md` and `squadB.md` were last touched 2026-07-14 — six weeks behind the actively 525 maintained rules files, though `conventions.md` and `typescript.md` are nominally older still. Of squadA's 21 526 territory paths, 4 exist; **zero** of squadB's 9 do. Both contradict `CODEOWNERS` on PDP 527 ownership — **CODEOWNERS says Squad B and is the one that enforces.** 528 529 ### Tier 1 approval 530 531 Four files are absolute: `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`. 532 Everything else Tier 1 is reachable under the verified-session exception — `gh api user`, check 533 `tier-1-approvers` membership, then name the file and the reason **in the commit body**. 534 535 Being Tier 1 is not by itself disqualifying; being one of the four named absolutes is. 536 537 ⚠️ **`tier-2-approvers` has 2 members and `tier-1-approvers` has 3.** Any PR touching 538 `theme/components/` is a two-person bus factor. 539 540 --- 541 542 ## Release, tagging and promotion 543 544 *New section.* 545 546 ### Tags 547 548 | Pattern | Who | Enforcement | 549 |---|---|---| 550 | `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | any developer | immutable for everyone | 551 | `vX.Y.Z` / `-hotfix.N` | tier-1-approvers only | creation restricted | 552 553 Always annotated (`-a -m`). Tag-only push — never `npm version`, which creates a 554 `package.json` commit that `release/**` protection blocks. 555 556 ⚠️ **Inverted:** a tier-1-approver *can* delete or move a final `vX.Y.Z` tag (the ruleset's 557 bypass is `always`, covering all its rules), while nobody can touch an `-rc.N`. That 558 contradicts the documented immutability guarantee. 559 560 ### Environments 561 562 **Continuous:** `dev` (every `develop` merge), `sit` (off the SIT gate on `release/**`). 563 **Tag-promoted:** `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` — `workflow_dispatch` with an explicit ref. 564 565 Plus an undocumented seventh surface: `deploy-preview.yml` auto-deploys ephemeral per-branch 566 MRT previews on every `feature/**`/`fix/**` push, excluding `fix/release-*`. Not in `tagging.md`'s model at all. 567 568 ### Three things to know before a release 569 570 1. **`prod`, `staging` and `uat` have zero protection rules.** Combined with `MRT_USER` / 571 `MRT_API_KEY` at repo scope, anyone with write access can dispatch `deploy-prod.yml` with 572 any ref and no human gate. `rollback=true` is documented as gated by required reviewers — 573 **there are none.** Setting them is the single highest-value fix available. 574 2. **A branch ref silently disarms the downgrade guard.** `check` *passes* on any non-version 575 ref and `record` *skips* it — and three of the four tag-promoted workflows default to a 576 branch. After any out-of-band deploy, re-run 577 `node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record ` or the guard's baseline is a lie. 578 3. **No `release/**` PR can merge today.** `SIT Gate` is required and admin-enforced; two of 579 `sit-gate`'s four required jobs cannot pass. `lighthouse-ci` has no server-start step and 580 `lighthouserc.js` falls back to `http://localhost:3000`, so it collects against a dead port — 581 provisioning the `LHCI_*` secrets alone will not fix it. `playwright-p0` selects 582 `--project=p0` against **zero `*.p0.spec` files**, with no `passWithNoTests`. Discover 583 this the week you cut `release/v0.1.0` and you're blocked on secrets provisioning, not code. 584 585 ⚠️ **`main` is the least-protected branch in the repo** — no test gate at all, and stale 586 reviews aren't dismissed. 587 588 ⚠️ **Three-way name divergence:** GitHub Environment (`staging`) ≠ workflow file (`stg`) ≠ MRT 589 target (`production` for prod). Tooling must key off the GitHub Environment name. 590 591 --- 592 593 ## Sprint, story and Jira/Confluence 594 595 *New section.* 596 597 ### Story decomposition 598 599 **Level 1 — component epics.** A PWA-Kit-only component gets one story. A Contentful + PWA-Kit 600 component gets **two** — one for the content model, one for rendering. 601 602 **Level 2 — page epics.** Shopper-perspective, how components work together. Must not repeat 603 Level-1 build detail. 604 605 Formalised in Confluence 04.71 (page 400195600). ⚠️ **Encoded nowhere in this repo** — nothing 606 in `.claude/`, `.docs/` or CI mentions or enforces it. 607 608 ### Cutting a UI story 609 610 1. **Slice by data source, not UI surface.** One story per tab is the wrong cut. 611 2. **Split again where risk differs** — unconfirmed attribute, unauthored content, unbuilt 612 integration. 613 3. **Every story a vertical slice.** Give a "shell" story a real first slice so it's demoable. 614 4. **Quarantine later-sprint work** (Hard Rule #14) and design for graceful degradation — 615 "renders now, wired later." 616 5. **Offer sub-tasks, not more stories,** when a BA wants finer granularity. 617 6. **Check the ticket against the PRD** and flag anything it assumes that's still open. 618 619 ### The Jira key 620 621 `SFCC-\d+`, hardcoded in three places that must stay in sync: `qa.yml:166`, 622 `runStoryTests.sh:43`, `computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs:47,55`. 623 624 **Not in the PR title** — conventional commits only. The Jira URL goes in the **body**, 625 manually, because the Forge app isn't installed. 626 627 ⚠️ **The two E2E tags fail differently.** A missing `@area` falls back to the full suite (safe). 628 A missing `@SFCC-NNN` means BrowserStack reports "no tests found" and **passes as a free 629 no-op** — a silent coverage hole. 630 631 ### ⚠️ `sprintScope.md` is two months stale and load-bearing 632 633 Last commit 2026-06-25. It says "Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress)" while its own table puts 634 today in Sprint 5. **AGENTS.md Hard Rule 14 makes it authoritative for scoping every task**, 635 and six skills cite it — so `/session-start`, `/feature-spec`, `/qa-generate` and `/onboarding` 636 all currently emit stale sprint context. Applied literally it would classify current PDP work 637 as past-sprint and trigger a stop-and-ask. 638 639 `projectState.md` is fresher but still lists SFCC-55 as "In Progress: PR #59" — that merged 640 2026-08-24 and is the head of `develop`. 641 642 **Jira is the only authority on the current sprint.** Don't derive it from the repo. 643 644 ### Confluence 645 646 Space key `SFCC`. Boundary rule: **source-of-truth or requirement → `.docs/`; how-to or process 647 doc for humans → Confluence.** 648 649 --- 650 651 ## Integration and vendor boundaries 652 653 *New section. `.docs/integration/` holds exactly 18 docs. The live/partial/doc-only split below 654 is a judgement from how much code each has in `overrides/`, not a reproducible count.* 655 656 **Live:** SFCC (SCAPI, SLAS auth) · Contentful. 657 658 **Partial:** MuleSoft (no proxy path in any config) · Booxi (falls back to a literal 659 `'https://BOOXI_BASE_URL'`) · Adyen (CSP and env done; the package isn't installed) · 660 Global-e (routing model only) · Google Maps · Measmerize (CSP done, no script injection). 661 662 **Doc-only:** Omneo · GiveX · reCAPTCHA · Narvar · Didomi · GTM · Inside Chat · Optimizely · 663 Crazy Egg · Vimeo. 664 665 ### Where the frontend boundary sits 666 667 **Tell No Lies** own GTM container contents, Optimizely experiments and Crazy Egg masking — 668 we emit the data layer, they consume it. **MuleSoft/Tryzens** own every PWA-direct read 669 endpoint. **The SFCC cartridge team** owns all Adyen server-side calls. **Booxi and Omneo** own 670 their APIs outright. **Zimmermann Privacy** owns all Didomi Console config — no consent rules 671 are hardcoded in the storefront. 672 673 **We own:** SCAPI consumption, Contentful rendering, the `dataLayer` emission contract, Consent 674 Mode translation, the script *loaders*, the MRT proxy legs, the Global-e `postMessage` listener, 675 Measmerize DOM containers — **and rendering payment/PII fields with stable maskable selectors 676 so TNL's config doesn't break between releases.** That last one looks like someone else's job 677 and isn't. 678 679 ### Four things that will bite 680 681 1. **`.env.sample` is the deployment schema, not documentation.** Only `# mrt:true`-tagged keys 682 sync to MRT, **from `.env.sample`**. `ADYEN_HMAC_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY`, 683 `BOOXI_BASE_URL` and `GTM_SERVER_URL` are named in docs and exist in no file — they will never reach MRT no matter how correct the code is. 684 2. **The Adyen HMAC failure mode is silent by design.** An absent key doesn't error — it 685 *downgrades* to Basic Auth and keeps accepting webhooks. Combined with #1, the default path 686 is an unauthenticated payment webhook that looks healthy in every log. 687 3. **Adding an MRT proxy path is a change to `config/` — one of the four absolutes.** Three 688 integrations are architected around proxy paths that don't exist. 689 4. **CSP is the silent gate on everything remaining, and it's mostly empty.** No entries for 690 Didomi, GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Vimeo, Omneo, Global-e or Narvar. And `useDefaults: true` 691 **replaces rather than merges** a directive, so partially editing an array silently drops the 692 rest. 693 694 ### Consent 695 696 **Fail closed.** If consent state is unknown, load nothing. The 5-second storefront timeout is a 697 *documented decision* (`.docs/integration/12-didomi.md:102`), explicitly not a Didomi-recommended 698 value — and it is **not implemented**: there is zero Didomi code under `overrides/`. 699 700 **Never silently substitute a different checkout, payment or commerce flow** when an 701 integration is down. Surface an explicit error. The sharpest case: never fall back to SFCC 702 checkout for an international destination — wrong flow, and tax/regulatory risk. 703 704 ⚠️ **Two integrations degrade in ways QA will file as defects:** reCAPTCHA gives zero bot 705 protection to a declining EU/UK visitor, and Narvar's EDD line vanishes silently. 706 707 --- 708 709 ## Who owns what 710 711 | Area | Working owner | 712 |---|---| 713 | Component conventions, reuse | you | 714 | Design tokens, Figma sign-off | UI designer | 715 | Story decomposition | BA, with your input | 716 | Content model / field IDs | you + Integration | 717 | CI/CD, env, secrets | Integration / SI | 718 | Release cut, final tags | tier-1-approvers | 719 | **Design-parity validation** | **unassigned — defaults to you** | 720 721 Run a boundary-setting session rather than discovering these one escalation at a time — and 722 put design-parity validation on its agenda explicitly. It is the only row with no owner, and an 723 unresourced ask that quietly becomes yours is the failure mode this table exists to prevent. 724 725 --- 726 727 ## Standing artifacts you own 728 729 | Artifact | Cadence | 730 |---|---| 731 | Component reuse register | per refinement | 732 | Token gap list | weekly, into design review | 733 | Estimation re-baseline | once, then per sprint | 734 | The three docs in this set | after each substantial build | 735 | Open-decisions list with owners | continuous | 736 737 --- 738 739 ## Current open items 740 741 1. **Set required reviewers on `prod`/`staging`/`uat`.** Highest-value fix available; 742 `rollback=true` is an ungated production bypass until then. 743 2. **`CODERABBIT_API_KEY` is a plaintext GitHub Actions *variable*** — 61 characters, 744 retrievable by any repo collaborator. So are `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (gates draft 745 content) and `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN`. The plaintext-variable mechanism is a documented, 746 accepted tradeoff for *public identifiers*; a live API key isn't one. 747 3. **Provision `LHCI_*` secrets and write one `*.p0.spec`** — until both exist, no release PR 748 can merge. 749 4. **Add `babel.config.js` and `tsconfig.json` to CODEOWNERS.** Declared Tier 1, enforced 750 nowhere. 751 5. **Reconcile `squadA.md`/`squadB.md` with CODEOWNERS**, or retire them. They contradict the 752 enforcing artefact on PDP ownership and mostly name paths that don't exist. 753 6. **Refresh `sprintScope.md`** or remove Hard Rule 14's dependency on it. 754 6b. **Two skill-layer traps that are still live:** `session-reflect.sh` forbids direct edits to 755 `.docs/memory/*` while `session-start` instructs them; and `/code-quality`'s default 756 `git diff --name-only main` fails outright in a checkout with no local `main` 757 (`/pr-checklist` correctly uses `develop`). 758 6c. **Terminology collision worth stating once to the team:** `new-component`'s "story" is a 759 Storybook file; `qa-generate`'s "story" is a Jira story becoming Gherkin. Same word, two 760 unrelated artifacts, two different audiences. 761 7. **Amend `overrideStyling.md`'s justification for dropping the `.zimm-btn-*` classes.** As 762 written it claims a static class *"can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/ 763 `_focusVisible`"* — **simply untrue of plain CSS**, and anyone who notices can dismiss the 764 whole rule. The real reasons are that two surfaces for one component drift, and a class 765 can't see the Chakra token layer. The conclusion is right; the stated reason is false. 766 7b. **Coordinate the F2R conversion before Han's 16 components land.** They sit at 767 `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/zimm-button/` (kebab, not camelCase) with co-located 768 `.styles.ts`. **Don't discard the `.styles.ts` files** — they're a faithful Figma→CSS 769 transcription and good raw material for a recipe. Convert them; don't copy the pattern. That 770 branch also predates PR #56 and carries its own `theme/foundation/`, so expect a real 771 conflict. 772 7c. **Settle `ui-kits` vs `uiKits`.** It's currently a silent exception to the camelCase rule. 773 Leave it undocumented and the next person adds `ui-kits/form-fields/`. 774 7d. **Reference `overrideStyling.md` from `AGENTS.md` and add it to 775 `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`'s manifest.** The largest rules file, holding the entire 776 styling hierarchy, is orphaned from the entry-point doc and invisible to Cursor and Copilot. 777 8. **Triage `audit:tokens`' 19 findings**, then wire it into CI. 778 9. **`promoteAlias.mjs:70` calls `environmentAlias.createOrUpdate`, which doesn't exist** in 779 `contentful-management@12.3.2` — 0 occurrences in the package. The production content 780 cutover script throws on its first real run. `bootstrapSpace.mjs:238-240` has the correct 781 pattern. 782 10. **Contentful content model exists only on `dev`.** Four tiers are empty; the template covers 783 5 of 14 types; there is no forward content promotion at all. 784 785 --- 786 787 *Revised 25 August 2026 against `develop` @ `8362b3c`. This pass absorbed 788 `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` (§3, §4) and added four sections: working with AI 789 tooling, release/tagging/promotion, sprint & Jira/Confluence, and integration boundaries. 790 Governance was expanded from a paragraph to a section after verification showed the rules files 791 and `CODEOWNERS` disagree on several paths — and that `CODEOWNERS`, which has no catch-all 792 rule, is the one that decides.* 793

file.content: # FED Lead Playbook **Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 · **Revised:** 25 August 2026 The lead role: what you say, to whom, and when. Judgement and process, not procedure. **Companions:** `fedBuild-manual.md` (how to build a component) · `uiBuild-knowledge.md` (why the machine behaves the way it does). **Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`. If this file disagrees with it, that file wins. *This document absorbed `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` (retired 25 Aug 2026). Its durable operating principles are §3; its training-vehicle material — a Next.js/Tailwind stack that isn't this one — was dropped.* --- ## 1. The mandate Sixteen responsibilities landed across two Contentful-vs-PWA-Kit alignment meetings. They reduce to two mandates: - **M1 — Protect the build.** Reuse, conventions, review, accessibility, performance. - **M2 — Protect the plan.** Estimation, scope, dependencies, escalation. **The one to resist as stated:** being a serial refinement gate across both squads. It won't scale and it will slip. Name that rather than absorbing it — an unresourced ask that quietly becomes yours is the failure mode here. ### The quality bar this serves The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3**, for the whole project. (Contract figure — nothing in `.docs/` records it, so cite the SOW itself, not the repo.) Three consequences: 1. **Vigilance is the job**, not an overhead on it. 2. **Budget real time per UI PR** — an hour or more. Principles *Absorbed from the retired playbook. These are the parts that survived contact with the codebase.* ### The quality ceiling is set by the human An AI assistant has no standards of its own — the standards and the constraints are things you supply. Its real value is making your assumptions visible faster, not making decisions. ### The dual mandate You hold two hats and the failure mode is collapsing into one. | | IC | Lead | |---|---|---| | Think | about the component | about the system | | Ask | until the spec is unambiguous | until the *team's* spec is unambiguous | | Decide | how to build it | whether it should be built now | | Review | your own output hardest | the pattern, not the line | | Protect | the build | the plan | | Multiply | — | the highest-leverage thing you do | **IC drift:** you're the only one who knows how something works. **Lead drift:** you haven't written code in a week and your review comments are getting vaguer. ### Defeating agreeableness An assistant that agrees with you is worth nothing. Four techniques that work: - **Role framing** — "you are a reviewer whose job is to find what's wrong with this." - **Steelman** — "give me the strongest argument *against* this approach." - **Critique-first** — ask for the problems before asking for the solution. - **Constraint injection** — name the constraint it must satisfy, so it can't hand-wave. Make it a team norm, not a private trick. ### Polishing is procrastination If an edit to a rules file didn't change what someone can or can't do, it wasn't a real edit. ### Define done, or nothing stops This applies to people and tools equally. "Improve the footer" has no terminal state. --- ## 4. Working with AI tooling *New section. The expensive failures on this project were not bad code — they were unrequested work and unrequested commits.* ### The authorisation ladder — three separate levels **Investigate ≠ fix ≠ commit.** "Run it" and "have a look" are investigation requests. They are not approval to change code, and changing code is not approval to commit it. Correct shape: **change → verify → stop and show the diff → wait.** This sharpens AGENTS.md Hard Rule #15 with the distinction the rule leaves implicit. Resuming from a session summary, a task list, or a "natural next step" is **not** an instruction to commit. ### The audit-loop failure mode A build can become a self-sustaining audit-and-fix cycle that feels productive and isn't. Measured on one stretch of SFCC-55: **55 commits, a 3.0:1 rework ratio, `footer/index.tsx` touched 32 times in 5 days.** The work wasn't wasted — it was mis-ordered. **The diagnostic that separates real work from generated work:** where did the finding come from? Six findings fixed things that were actually broken. Seven came from *reading code we'd just written*. If a finding's origin is your own fresh output rather than a spec, a reproduced failure, or a review comment, it is probably not the next thing to do. Two correctives: - **Read the review queue before starting a self-directed pass.** A six-hour-old Major finding named a live security bypass while the loop was polishing comment placement. - **Ban "it's good practice" as a justification.** A fix needs a named requirement, a reproduced failure, or a review comment behind it. ### Present verdicts, don't auto-fix When a pass produces a list of possible improvements, separate the ones traceable to a spec/failure/review from the ones traceable to your own just-written code — and **offer** the second group rather than doing them. ### Don't take an agent's report at face value Two agent claims were overturned by direct verification in a single session this week: that a11y is ungated (it is gated — the agent was reasoning from Storybook 8), and that the CLI would work with the repo's management token (it reads neither that env var nor any other). When a local doc is the real reason for a decision, find the public equivalent in `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/` or `.docs/` and cite that. If none exists, argue the merits directly. Four rules that follow from that: - **Deploy first.** A thing that runs somewhere other than your machine is the only evidence that counts. - **Partial-but-hardened beats complete-but-broken.** Three states done properly ships; six states half-wired doesn't. - **Descope, never cut quality.** Cutting the loading state to hit a date converts a schedule problem into a defect-budget problem, and the budget is smaller. - **The 20-minute rule.** Twenty minutes without progress is a signal to change approach or ask, not to push harder. ### Three states are AC, not polish Every component that renders fetched data needs **loading** (a skeleton, not a spinner), **error** (with retry), and **absent** (see `uiBuild-knowledge.md` §7) specified in the story. The 5-second storefront timeout is a *documented decision* (`.docs/integration/12-didomi.md:102`), explicitly not a Didomi-recommended value — and it is **not implemented**: there is zero Didomi code under `overrides/`. **Never silently substitute a different checkout, payment or commerce flow** when an integration is down. Surface an explicit error. The sharpest case: never fall back to SFCC checkout for an international destination — wrong flow, and tax/regulatory risk. ⚠️ **Two integrations degrade in ways QA will file as defects:** reCAPTCHA gives zero bot protection to a declining EU/UK visitor, and Narvar's EDD line vanishes silently. --- ## Who owns what | Area | Working owner | |---|---| | Component conventions, reuse | you | | Design tokens, Figma sign-off | UI designer | | Story decomposition | BA, with your input | | Content model / field IDs | you + Integration | | CI/CD, env, secrets | Integration / SI | | Release cut, final tags | tier-1-approvers | | **Design-parity validation** | **unassigned — defaults to you** | Run a boundary-setting session rather than discovering these one escalation at a time — and put design-parity validation on its agenda explicitly. It is the only row with no owner, and an unresourced ask that quietly becomes yours is the failure mode this table exists to prevent. --- ## Standing artifacts you own | Artifact | Cadence | |---|---| | Component reuse register | per refinement | | Token gap list | weekly, into design review | | Estimation re-baseline | once, then per sprint | | The three docs in this set | after each substantial build | | Open-decisions list with owners | continuous | --- ## Current open items 1. **Set required reviewers on `prod`/`staging`/`uat`.** Highest-value fix available; `rollback=true` is an ungated production bypass until then. 2. **`CODERABBIT_API_KEY` is a plaintext GitHub Actions *variable*** — 61 characters, retrievable by any repo collaborator. So are `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (gates draft content) and `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN`. The plaintext-variable mechanism is a documented, accepted tradeoff for *public identifiers*; a live API key isn't one. 3. **Provision `LHCI_*` secrets and write one `*.p0.spec`** — until both exist, no release PR can merge. 4. **Add `babel.config.js` and `tsconfig.json` to CODEOWNERS.** Declared Tier 1, enforced nowhere. 5. **Reconcile `squadA.md`/`squadB.md` with CODEOWNERS**, or retire them. They contradict the enforcing artefact on PDP ownership and mostly name paths that don't exist. 6. **Refresh `sprintScope.md`** or remove Hard Rule 14's dependency on it. 6b. **Two skill-layer traps that are still live:** `session-reflect.sh` forbids direct edits to `.docs/memory/*` while `session-start` instructs them; and `/code-quality`'s default `git diff --name-only main` fails outright in a checkout with no local `main` (`/pr-checklist` correctly uses `develop`). 6c. **Terminology collision worth stating once to the team:** `new-component`'s "story" is a Storybook file; `qa-generate`'s "story" is a Jira story becoming Gherkin. Same word, two unrelated artifacts, two different audiences. 7. **Amend `overrideStyling.md`'s justification for dropping the `.zimm-btn-*` classes.** As written it claims a static class *"can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/ `_focusVisible`"* — **simply untrue of plain CSS**, and anyone who notices can dismiss the whole rule. The real reasons are that two surfaces for one component drift, and a class can't see the Chakra token layer. The conclusion is right; the stated reason is false. 7b. **Coordinate the F2R conversion before Han's 16 components land.** They sit at `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/zimm-button/` (kebab, not camelCase) with co-located `.styles.ts`. **Don't discard the `.styles.ts` files** — they're a faithful Figma→CSS transcription and good raw material for a recipe. Convert them; don't copy the pattern. That branch also predates PR #56 and carries its own `theme/foundation/`, so expect a real conflict. 7c. **Settle `ui-kits` vs `uiKits`.** It's currently a silent exception to the camelCase rule. Leave it undocumented and the next person adds `ui-kits/form-fields/`. 7d. **Reference `overrideStyling.md` from `AGENTS.md` and add it to `scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs`'s manifest.** The largest rules file, holding the entire styling hierarchy, is orphaned from the entry-point doc and invisible to Cursor and Copilot. 8. **Triage `audit:tokens`' 19 findings**, then wire it into CI. 9. **`promoteAlias.mjs:70` calls `environmentAlias.createOrUpdate`, which doesn't exist** in `contentful-management@12.3.2` — 0 occurrences in the package. The production content cutover script throws on its first real run. `bootstrapSpace.mjs:238-240` has the correct pattern. 10. **Contentful content model exists only on `dev`.** Four tiers are empty; the template covers 5 of 14 types; there is no forward content promotion at all. --- *Revised 25 August 2026 against `develop` @ `8362b3c`. This pass absorbed `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` (§3, §4) and added four sections: working with AI tooling, release/tagging/promotion, sprint & Jira/Confluence, and integration boundaries. Governance was expanded from a paragraph to a section after verification showed the rules files and `CODEOWNERS` disagree on several paths — and that `CODEOWNERS`, which has no catch-all rule, is the one that decides.*
