1	# Styling an Override Component
2	
3	How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
4	Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
5	different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
6	about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
7	rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
8	companion.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## The hierarchy — reach for these in order
13	
14	1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
15	   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
16	2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
17	   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
18	   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
19	   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
20	   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
21	   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
22	   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
23	   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
24	   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
25	   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
26	   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
27	   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
28	3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
29	   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
30	   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
31	   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
32	   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
33	   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
34	   type" below.
35	4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
36	5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
37	   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.
38	
39	**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
40	instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
41	constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
42	sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
43	before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
44	`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
45	(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
46	from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
47	contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
48	the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
49	existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
50	2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
51	full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
52	genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
53	Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
54	mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
55	Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
56	which is what `audit:tokens` is for.
57	
58	## Units
59	
60	- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
61	  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
62	  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
63	  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
64	  comment for traceability.
65	- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
66	  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
67	  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
68	- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
69	  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
70	  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.
71	
72	## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy
73	
74	`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
75	plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
76	...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
77	value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
78	if only one of them is ever typed.
79	
80	`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
81	classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
82	`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
83	from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
84	numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
85	`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
86	derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
87	regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.
88	
89	## One canonical styling surface per component type
90	
91	Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
92	either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
93	beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
94	`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
95	`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
96	`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
97	structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
98	with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
99	button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
100	for any button, not a class.
101	
102	`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
103	massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
104	there's no interactive state to lose.
105	
106	## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component
107	
108	If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
109	override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
110	(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
111	(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
112	base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
113	that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
114	import, which is correct for that file).
115	
116	The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
117	`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
118	`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
119	server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
120	`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
121	resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
122	correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
123	version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
124	override and isn't.
125	
126	**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
127	import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
128	the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
129	calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
130	worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.
131	
132	An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
133	overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
134	etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.
135	
136	## Component-local tokens
137	
138	When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
139	`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
140	— `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
141	`marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
142	form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
143	used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
144	`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
145	so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.
146	
147	See `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` and
148	`.../footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` for the pattern in a real recipe. The reason is
149	traceability, not parity with the base theme: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference names the
150	Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these
151	recipes are deliberately namespaced `ZimmFooter*` so they do **not** inherit the base
152	SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
153	numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)
154	
155	**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
156	co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:
157	
158	```ts
159	[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
160	```
161	
162	The array shorthand (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`) is what this section used to
163	recommend, and it would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks
164	responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail.
165	`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.
166	
167	When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
168	have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
169	than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
170	`header.ts`/`zimmButton.css.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
171	sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.
172	
173	## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)
174	
175	If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
176	"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
177	node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
178	faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
179	matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put
180	Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default and adds
181	brand-specific defaults, the same split `product-tile/index.tsx` (`CardBaseline`
182	name + default) and `link/index.tsx` already use. `image-gallery`, `display-price`, and
183	`swatch-group` are all shared internal SFCC dependencies. When one of them does get
184	overridden, keep its default export API-compatible and put brand styling in a theme
185	recipe rather than a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't require a second
186	export the way `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.
187	
188	**As of `7b9b5dc`, none of the three is overridden at all** — no component override, no
189	theme recipe, nothing registered for them in `theme/components/index.ts`. Verify current
190	state before relying on any of this. `protectedFiles.md` and `CODEOWNERS` list those
191	paths forward-lookingly, not descriptively. An earlier revision of this paragraph cited
192	`theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` as holding their styling; neither
193	file has ever existed on any branch.
194	
195	---
196	
197	## Co-locating a component's theme file
198	
199	A component's recipe may live beside it as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g.
200	`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, or an organism's own
201	`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/<name>/<name>.css.ts`) instead of in
202	`theme/components/`. Either way it's still registered in
203	`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key
204	passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path, so co-location is purely an
205	organisational choice with no runtime difference.
206	
207	**Governance follows the file, not the folder.** `theme/components/` is Tier 2, gated to
208	the UI designer (protectedFiles.md). A co-located `<name>.css.ts` is deliberately routed
209	differently: CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule sends it to the
210	owning squad(s) only, dropping the Tier 1/2 approver requirement that the surrounding
211	directory (e.g. `header/`, `footer/`) otherwise carries. That's intentional — a co-located
212	file is for composing a component's own layout from **already-established** tokens
213	(spacing, colour, typography scale), not for authoring new raw design values. Authoring an
214	actual new token still means editing `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a `theme/components/`
215	recipe that's still designer-owned (`header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts` — the
216	files that remain in that directory) — both stay behind the full gate.
217	
218	> **Known inconsistency, flagged not resolved.** This paragraph used to cite `button.ts`'s
219	> `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y` as the designer-gated example. That file
220	> is now `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`, which the `**/*.css.ts` rule above
221	> routes to the squads — so those provisional, unapproved constants are **no longer
222	> designer-gated**, while still keying the app-wide `Button` recipe. The example was swapped
223	> to `header.ts` (genuinely still gated) so this paragraph stops asserting something false.
224	> Whether `zimmButton.css.ts` should be re-gated is an open governance question, not a doc
225	> fix, and is deliberately left open here.
226	
227	**Enforcement gap, partially closed:** the Tier 1/2 human reviewer was, until this rule
228	existed, the only thing catching a hardcoded hex/px/rem/em value landing in a theme file.
229	`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (`npm run audit:tokens`, see the `Never` note above) now exists
230	and runs correctly against the real codebase — built 2026-08-23. What's still open: it is not
231	wired into CI, so it only catches something if a developer or reviewer remembers to run it —
232	removing the Tier 1/2 reviewer from co-located `.css.ts` files still removes an *automatic*
233	backstop for exactly the files most likely to need it. Wiring `audit:tokens` as a required CI
234	check on `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` is the remaining near-term follow-up, not an
235	optional nice-to-have — and per the script's own header, someone should triage a full run's
236	findings first (14 pre-existing, unrelated violations turned up the day it was built) before
237	turning it into a hard gate.
238	
239	**Cross-file shared values** (a breakpoint or provisional size needed by more than one
240	split-out file) go in a small shared module that stays in `theme/components/` — e.g.
241	`footerShared.ts`, holding the breakpoints and the one size value `footerNavColumn.css.ts`
242	and `bottomBar.css.ts` both need. Don't copy the same literal into two co-located files;
243	that's exactly the drift risk "The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy" (above)
244	already warns about.
245	
246	**Reference example:** the footer decomposition (SFCC-55 follow-up) split
247	`theme/components/footer.ts`'s 33 parts across `footer/footer.css.ts` (shell),
248	`footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts`, `footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts`, and
249	three `ui-kits/organisms/`/`ui-kits/molecules/` recipes — with `footerShared.ts` left
250	behind in `theme/components/` for the two genuinely cross-file values.
251	
252	## Known gaps (not silently dropped — logged here)
253	
254	- The f2r `zimm-product-detail-options` prototype spec includes a size-as-dropdown
255	  picker, a wishlist button, a "find in boutique" link, and description/shipping
256	  accordions. None of those exist as overrides yet, so `ProductDetailOptions` ships
257	  without them — it's colour/size swatches, quantity, and add-to-bag only.
258	- `swatch-group`'s `square`/`circle` variant functions (selected/disabled colour logic,
259	  the diagonal disabled-state gradient) are still inherited from the base SFCC theme —
260	  real visual design decisions with no Zimmermann Figma spec behind them yet.
261	- `zimmButton.css.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px) disagree with the
262	  Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px) — flagged in `zimmButton.css.ts`,
263	  pending UI-designer sign-off. `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all —
264	  a gap to fill, not a conflict to resolve.
265	- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` is claimed by `.claude/rules/squadA.md`
266	  (draft, scope still settling) — flagged for awareness, not treated as a hard block.
267	
268	## Follow-up work (separate initiatives)
269	
270	- **Per-component CSS loading.** `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*` class registry is
271	  registered as one `theme.styles.global` block and ships on every page regardless of
272	  which classes a given page's components actually use. If component overrides start
273	  applying `.zimm-*` classNames directly for the non-interactive cases described above,
274	  only the classes a page's components actually reference should load, not the whole
275	  registry. Needs its own investigation, not scoped or estimated yet.
276	- **`globalStyles.ts` adoption is currently near zero.** Of the classes still defined
277	  there, none have a real consumer anywhere in the app today except one Storybook demo
278	  (`spacing.stories.tsx`'s `.zimm-grid` example). They're Handover-ported 1:1 and
279	  presumably _intended_ to be reused, just not adopted by any component yet — worth
280	  revisiting once component overrides actually start applying them.

---

2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
   type" below.
4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.

**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
which is what `audit:tokens` is for.

## Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
  comment for traceability.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy

`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
if only one of them is ever typed.

`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.

## One canonical styling surface per component type

Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
there's no interactive state to lose.

## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component

If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import, which is correct for that file).

The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
override and isn't.

**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.

An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.

## Component-local tokens

When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
— `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
`marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.

See `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` and
`.../footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` for the pattern in a real recipe. The reason is
traceability, not parity with the base theme: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference names the
Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these
recipes are deliberately namespaced `ZimmFooter*` so they do **not** inherit the base
SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)

**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

The array shorthand (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`) is what this section used to
recommend, and it would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks
responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail.
`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.

When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
`header.ts`/`zimmButton.css.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.

## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)

If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put
Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default and adds
brand-specific defaults, the same split `product-tile/index.tsx` (`CardBaseline`
name + default) and `link/index.tsx` already use. `image-gallery`, `display-price`, and
`swatch-group` are all shared internal SFCC dependencies. When one of them does get
overridden, keep its default export API-compatible and put brand styling in a theme
recipe rather than a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't require a second
export the way `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.

**As of `7b9b5dc`, none of the three is overridden at all** — no component override, no
theme recipe, nothing registered for them in `theme/components/index.ts`. Verify current
state before relying on any of this. `protectedFiles.md` and `CODEOWNERS` list those
paths forward-lookingly, not descriptively. An earlier revision of this paragraph cited
`theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` as holding their styling; neither
file has ever existed on any branch.

---

## Co-locating a component's theme file

A component's recipe may live beside it as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g.
`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, or an organism's own
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/<name>/<name>.css.ts`) instead of in
`theme/components/`. Either way it's still registered in
`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key
passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path, so co-location is purely an
organisational choice with no runtime difference.

**Governance follows the file, not the folder.** `theme/components/` is Tier 2, gated to
the UI designer (protectedFiles.md). A co-located `<name>.css.ts` is deliberately routed
differently: CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule sends it to the
owning squad(s) only, dropping the Tier 1/2 approver requirement that the surrounding
directory (e.g. `header/`, `footer/`) otherwise carries. That's intentional — a co-located
file is for composing a component's own layout from **already-established** tokens
(spacing, colour, typography scale), not for authoring new raw design values. Authoring an
actual new token still means editing `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a `theme/components/`
recipe that's still designer-owned (`header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts` — the
files that remain in that directory) — both stay behind the full gate.

> **Known inconsistency, flagged not resolved.** This paragraph used to cite `button.ts`'s
> `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y` as the designer-gated example. That file
> is now `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`, which the `**/*.css.ts` rule above
> routes to the squads — so those provisional, unapproved constants are **no longer
> designer-gated**, while still keying the app-wide `Button` recipe. The example was swapped
> to `header.ts` (genuinely still gated) so this paragraph stops asserting something false.
> Whether `zimmButton.css.ts` should be re-gated is an open governance question, not a doc
> fix, and is deliberately left open here.

**Enforcement gap, partially closed:** the Tier 1/2 human reviewer was, until this rule
existed, the only thing catching a hardcoded hex/px/rem/em value landing in a theme file.
`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (`npm run audit:tokens`, see the `Never` note above) now exists
and runs correctly against the real codebase — built 2026-08-23. What's still open: it is not
wired into CI, so it only catches something if a developer or reviewer remembers to run it —
removing the Tier 1/2 reviewer from co-located `.css.ts` files still removes an *automatic*
backstop for exactly the files most likely to need it. Wiring `audit:tokens` as a required CI
check on `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` is the remaining near-term follow-up, not an
optional nice-to-have — and per the script's own header, someone should triage a full run's
findings first (14 pre-existing, unrelated violations turned up the day it was built) before
turning it into a hard gate.

**Cross-file shared values** (a breakpoint or provisional size needed by more than one
split-out file) go in a small shared module that stays in `theme/components/` — e.g.
`footerShared.ts`, holding the breakpoints and the one size value `footerNavColumn.css.ts`
and `bottomBar.css.ts` both need. Don't copy the same literal into two co-located files;
that's exactly the drift risk "The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy" (above)
already warns about.

**Reference example:** the footer decomposition (SFCC-55 follow-up) split
`theme/components/footer.ts`'s 33 parts across `footer/footer.css.ts` (shell),
`footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts`, `footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts`, and
three `ui-kits/organisms/`/`ui-kits/molecules/` recipes — with `footerShared.ts` left
behind in `theme/components/` for the two genuinely cross-file values.

## Known gaps (not silently dropped — logged here)

- The f2r `zimm-product-detail-options` prototype spec includes a size-as-dropdown
  picker, a wishlist button, a "find in boutique" link, and description/shipping
  accordions. None of those exist as overrides yet, so `ProductDetailOptions` ships
  without them — it's colour/size swatches, quantity, and add-to-bag only.
- `swatch-group`'s `square`/`circle` variant functions (selected/disabled colour logic,
  the diagonal disabled-state gradient) are still inherited from the base SFCC theme —
  real visual design decisions with no Zimmermann Figma spec behind them yet.
- `zimmButton.css.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px) disagree with the
  Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px) — flagged in `zimmButton.css.ts`,
  pending UI-designer sign-off. `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all —
  a gap to fill, not a conflict to resolve.
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` is claimed by `.claude/rules/squadA.md`
  (draft, scope still settling) — flagged for awareness, not treated as a hard block.

## Follow-up work (separate initiatives)

- **Per-component CSS loading.** `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*` class registry is
  registered as one `theme.styles.global` block and ships on every page regardless of
  which classes a given page's components actually use. If component overrides start
  applying `.zimm-*` classNames directly for the non-interactive cases described above,
  only the classes a page's components actually reference should load, not the whole
  registry. Needs its own investigation, not scoped or estimated yet.
- **`globalStyles.ts` adoption is currently near zero.** Of the classes still defined
  there, none have a real consumer anywhere in the app today except one Storybook demo
  (`spacing.stories.tsx`'s `.zimm-grid` example). They're Handover-ported 1:1 and
  presumably _intended_ to be reused, just not adopted by any component yet — worth
  revisiting once component overrides actually start applying them.

# CSS & Styling Conventions

Chakra UI and `.scss` conventions. See [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Rules > Styling for the
higher-level policy (Chakra props first, `.scss` only when insufficient, theme file
ownership/tiers) — this file covers the concrete day-to-day rules underneath that policy.

---

## Tokens — no hardcoded design values

Chakra UI props must use the Chakra token system — no hardcoded hex colours, no pixel
values for spacing, no raw font sizes. Tokens belong in
[overrides/app/theme/foundation/](../../overrides/app/theme/) (Tier 1 — see
[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)).

```tsx
// ❌ hardcoded
<Box color="#1A1A1A" padding="16px" />

// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string — resolves correctly (theme.colors/theme.space ARE
// registered from the Zimmermann foundations) but is still not allowed in an override
// component; see overrideStyling.md's hierarchy point 2 for why
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ token, as a raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

Type is its own case, not shown above — set it with `textStyle` (`textStyle="body2"`), never
a raw `fontSize`, per [overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md) point 1. There's no
`var(--zimm-*)` substitute for the composite `textStyle` expansion itself, only for its
individual pieces (`var(--zimm-font-size-*)` etc.), so `textStyle` stays a bare key —
it's the one entry in the hierarchy that isn't a colour/spacing token.

**The raw-hex/px/rem/em half of this has a script but no CI gate yet.**
`npm run audit:tokens` (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`) scans `overrides/app/components/**`
and `overrides/app/theme/components/**` for exactly this — see
[overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md)'s `Never` note for the full scope and its
acknowledged-exception rules. It's not wired into CI (no `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` rule
either), so nothing blocks a merge that skips running it — that's still a real gap, just not
an unstarted one.
The bare-token-vs-`var(--zimm-*)` half above **is** mechanically enforced for recipe files —
see `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`, which runs on every `npm run test` — though it
can't see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop; that half still relies on review.

---

## `.scss` — only when Chakra props are insufficient

Per AGENTS.md, reach for a `.scss` file alongside a component only when Chakra's prop system
genuinely can't express what's needed (e.g. complex pseudo-selectors, keyframe animations,
print styles). When you do:

- **File naming:** matches the component file exactly — `productTile.scss` next to
  `productTile/index.tsx` (see [conventions.md](./conventions.md) > File naming and folder
  structure for the folder layout this sits in).
- **Scoped, co-located only.** No global stylesheets outside `overrides/app/theme/` — a
  component's `.scss` file must only affect that component's own markup.
- **Nesting depth ≤ 3 levels.** Beyond that, the selector is almost always reaching into a
  child component's internals rather than styling its own root — a sign the styling belongs
  in that child instead, or that Chakra's `sx` prop / a theme variant would express it more
  directly.
- **No ID selectors.** Class-based only — an ID selector's specificity makes it
  disproportionately hard to override later (including by a legitimate future Chakra
  variant), and IDs aren't guaranteed unique when a component renders more than once on a
  page.
- **No `!important`** without an inline comment explaining why the override is genuinely
  unavoidable (e.g. fighting a third-party widget's inline styles) — same reasoning as the
  `any`/non-null-assertion escape hatches in [typescript.md](./typescript.md): allowed, but
  the reason has to be visible at the point of use, not left for the next reader to guess.
- **Prefer Chakra's `sx` prop or a theme variant extension over a new `.scss` file** for
  anything that's really just "a Chakra style the prop system doesn't have a named prop for"
  — a new global class is a bigger footprint than a one-off `sx` override, and `sx` keeps the
  style co-located with the JSX that uses it instead of a separate file to keep in sync.

1	# Testing Conventions
2	
3	Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.
4	
5	**This is not license to skip a component's own test file because its behaviour happens to be
6	covered transitively elsewhere.** A component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping
7	decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx`, even when the state it
8	renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test, or a parent's assembly-level
9	Storybook `play` already exercises the rendered result. Resolve the duplication concern by
10	**scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven
11	elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract (given a state, does it render the
12	right branch; given a DOM event, does it call the right handler) — not by leaving the
13	component with no test of its own. Relying on a *different* component's story to prove *this*
14	component's contract means the coverage isn't discoverable from the component's own folder,
15	and can silently vanish if that unrelated file changes. See
16	`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for the
17	resulting pattern (mocks `useSubscribeSection` and `ZimmSubscribeModal`, tests only its own
18	render-branch/event-wiring contract). A component with no branching or decision logic at all
19	(pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`) still doesn't need its own suite — the exemption
20	below for single-parent internal components still applies there.
21	
22	| Layer | Tool | What it covers | File pattern | CI gate |
23	|---|---|---|---|---|
24	| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, hook behaviour in isolation | `*.test.ts` co-located with the source | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
25	| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | User-facing interactions in a single component (clicks, form fills, focus management) | `*.stories.tsx` `play` function | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
26	| E2E | Playwright | Full user journeys across pages, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,js}` | Every PR (`qa.yml`) — desktop + mobile Chromium against localhost/dev API; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**` only |
27	
28	> Higher-level project rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing. Day-to-day file conventions: [conventions.md](./conventions.md). This file describes **how** to write tests at each layer.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## What to test (and what to skip)
33	
34	Write tests where failure would be **non-obvious** or **costly to debug**:
35	
36	- ✅ Data mapping: Contentful → component props, locale/currency transforms, SFCC payload → view model
37	- ✅ Integration boundaries: Global-e pricing/tax logic, checkout ownership branching, consent gating
38	- ✅ Complex state: cart mutations, consent state changes, multi-step flows, optimistic-update rollback
39	- ✅ Pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken
40	- ❌ Re-exports, one-line passthroughs, type-only helpers
41	- ❌ Storybook visual snapshots — Chromatic/Loki belongs in a separate budget, not Vitest
42	- ❌ The framework — don't test that React renders, that Chakra applies styles, or that React Query caches
43	
44	---
45	
46	## Layer 1 — Vitest (unit)
47	
48	### File layout
49	
50	Co-located with the source, `.test.ts` suffix, never `.spec.ts`:
51	
52	```
53	overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.ts
54	overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.test.ts
55	overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.ts
56	overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.test.ts
57	```
58	
59	Components use `index.test.ts` next to `index.tsx` in the component folder
60	(see [components.md](./components.md) > Components).
61	
62	### Structure
63	
64	- `describe` blocks group related cases; `test` (or `it`) for individual cases.
65	- **Arrange → Act → Assert** pattern, one behaviour per test.
66	- Test names describe the behaviour, not the implementation: `"converts AUD to USD using the latest Global-e rate"` not `"calls convertCurrency"`.
67	- Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test.
68	
69	### Mocking
70	
71	- **Inline mock objects** for isolated unit tests — define plain JS objects right in the test file.
72	- **`vi.mock()`** for module-level stubs. Mock the smallest possible surface: a single function, not a whole module, when feasible.
73	- **MSW** is allowed for cross-functional integration tests (multiple modules wired together). Production paths must never depend on MSW — see AGENTS.md > Rules > "No mocking."
74	- Do not mock the thing under test; do not assert on internal implementation calls when an output assertion would do.
75	- **Known gap: `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel
76	  (`app/components/icons`), which has a top-level side effect (`AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...`)
77	  that fails here because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings in this environment, not
78	  components. Not fixable from a test file — the SVG transform lives in `vitest.config.ts`,
79	  Tier 1 test config (AGENTS.md Hard Rule 8). Work around it by mocking `ZimmIcon` at the
80	  smallest surface in any test that renders an icon-consuming component:
81	  `vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))` — or,
82	  if an assertion depends on an accessible name the real `ZimmIcon` would carry (e.g. a
83	  fallback `<span aria-label>` with no wrapping interactive element), forward the relevant
84	  props instead of returning `null`. See `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` and
85	  `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for both variants.
86	
87	### Commerce SDK hooks
88	
89	Hooks that call `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (e.g. `useCurrentBasket`, `useCurrentCustomer`) need a `QueryClientProvider` and `CommerceApiProvider` wrapper. Build a small `renderWithProviders` helper in `overrides/app/test-utils/` rather than duplicating wrapper boilerplate per test.
90	
91	### What NOT to write at this layer
92	
93	- Visual rendering — that's Storybook
94	- Cross-page navigation — that's Playwright
95	- Real network calls — never; use MSW or stubbed hooks
96	
97	---
98	
99	## Layer 2 — Storybook `play` (component interaction)
100	
101	### When to use `play`
102	
103	Every UI component has a `*.stories.tsx` (see [components.md](./components.md) > Storybook). Add a `play` function when there is **interactive behaviour worth asserting**:
104	
105	- Form validation triggers on blur / submit
106	- Disclosure (accordion, drawer, modal) opens / closes via keyboard + mouse
107	- Focus moves correctly through a flow
108	- A controlled input's onChange wires through to the rendered output
109	
110	If the story is purely visual (renders different prop combinations), no `play` is needed.
111	
112	### Pattern
113	
114	```tsx
115	import {expect, userEvent, within} from '@storybook/test'
116	
117	export const SubmitDisabledUntilValid: Story = {
118	    play: async ({canvasElement}) => {
119	        const canvas = within(canvasElement)
120	        const submit = canvas.getByRole('button', {name: /submit/i})
121	        await expect(submit).toBeDisabled()
122	        await userEvent.type(canvas.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'name@example.com')
123	        await expect(submit).toBeEnabled()
124	    }
125	}
126	```
127	
128	- Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly.
129	- Use **`getByRole`** with an accessible name as the first-choice selector. Fall back to `getByLabelText` for form fields, `getByText` last.
130	- Don't import `userEvent` from `@testing-library/user-event` — use the Storybook re-export so the action is logged in the timeline.
131	
132	### What NOT to write at this layer
133	
134	- Multi-page flows — that's Playwright
135	- Heavy API mocking — keep stories visual, push integration assertions to Playwright
136	
137	---
138	
139	## Layer 3 — Playwright (E2E)
140	
141	### Workflow
142	
143	E2E tests follow the **three-stage gherkin-first workflow** (see [.claude/skills/qa-generate/](../skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md)):
144	
145	1. Claude (or any developer) drafts a `.feature` file with Gherkin scenarios
146	2. Lead QA validates in plain English — **no Playwright code is written until sign-off**
147	3. Playwright spec is generated only after the `.feature` is approved
148	
149	This prevents "technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour."
150	
151	### File layout
152	
153	```
154	e2e/features/         # Gherkin .feature files — source of truth, reviewed by Lead QA
155	e2e/fixtures/         # multi-region fixtures keyed by SITE_ID
156	e2e/support/
157	  helpers/            # shared helpers (auth, basket setup)
158	  pages/              # Page Object Model classes (BasePage, CheckoutPage, …)
159	e2e/tests/zimm/       # generated Playwright specs, mirroring features/
160	```
161	
162	Spec filename convention for story-backed specs: `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`
163	(`.p0.` runs in the Digital SIT gate on `release/**`; on a `develop`-targeted PR, `e2e-localhost`
164	runs only the specs relevant to the diff — see **Change-scoped E2E** below). Jira-less smoke
165	tests use `SMOKE-{area}-{behaviour}.spec.js` instead — see
166	[e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests.
167	
168	### Change-scoped E2E (`develop`-targeted PRs only)
169	
170	`e2e-localhost` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) narrows which specs it runs based on the changed
171	files in the diff, instead of always running the full suite:
172	
173	- Every spec must carry a Playwright test tag matching its Gherkin file's `@area` tag (see
174	  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) for the tag list — `homepage`,
175	  `checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations`) — and, per **BrowserStack story
176	  scoping** below, its `@SFCC-NNN` tag too: `test('...', {tag: ['@homepage', '@SFCC-142']}, async
177	  ({page}) => {...})`. Smoke tests (no Jira story — see
178	  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests) are exempt from the
179	  `@SFCC-NNN` half of this — `@area @smoke` only.
180	- `detect-changes`'s `Get changed files` step defines one file-path allow-list per area
181	  (`e2e_homepage`, and so on as new areas get specs). `Compute E2E scope` narrows the run to
182	  that area's `--grep` tag **only if every e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that one
183	  area's allow-list** — a single file outside it (a shared/global path, or one no area has
184	  claimed yet) falls back to the full suite, deliberately, rather than needing its own
185	  deny-list to maintain. `qa.yml`'s inline comments are the source of truth for the exact path
186	  lists — don't duplicate them here, they'll drift.
187	- `release/**`-targeted PRs always run the full suite regardless of diff — this narrowing only
188	  applies to `develop`-targeted PRs.
189	- **Adding a new area's first spec:** give it its own allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s
190	  `detect-changes` job, tag every `test()` in it with the matching `{tag: '@area'}`, and add it
191	  to this section. Forgetting either step doesn't lose coverage — an untagged/unmapped spec
192	  still runs under the full-suite fallback — it just misses out on the scoping optimisation.
193	
194	### BrowserStack story scoping
195	
196	`e2e-browserstack` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a
197	general regression gate — that's what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for.
198	
199	- **`release/**`-targeted PRs:** always run the full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite, unscoped. A
200	  release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply — Zephyr
201	  traceability still works, since every test carries its own `@SFCC-NNN` tag individually.
202	- **`develop`-targeted PRs:** `detect-changes`'s `Detect Jira story keys` step regexes
203	  `SFCC-\d+` out of the PR title, PR body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-
204	  Jira app uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own. If
205	  at least one key is found, `e2e-browserstack` runs `--grep`-scoped to that story's tag(s)
206	  (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job doesn't run at
207	  all.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results to in Zephyr, there's
208	  nothing correct to run.
209	- If a key is found but no spec carries the matching `@SFCC-NNN` tag, `--grep` matches zero
210	  tests and Playwright reports "no tests found" without spinning up any BrowserStack sessions
211	  — a free no-op, not a failure, and not something that falls back to a full run.
212	- Every story-backed spec needs its Jira key as a tag alongside its `@area` tag (see
213	  **Change-scoped E2E** above) for this to work — the `qa-generate` skill adds both
214	  automatically. Jira-less smoke tests (`@area @smoke` only) never match a story key, so they
215	  correctly never run under BrowserStack — that's expected, not a gap; they're already covered
216	  by `e2e-localhost`.
217	- **Local pre-push equivalent:** `npm run test:story` (`scripts/runStoryTests.sh`) runs the
218	  same `browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep` command against real
219	  BrowserStack, so a developer can exercise their story before opening the PR. Pass the key
220	  explicitly (`npm run test:story -- SFCC-142`) or let it auto-detect from commit messages on
221	  the branch and the branch name — the same `SFCC-\d+` pattern, applied to local git state
222	  instead of PR title/body since no PR exists yet at that point. Requires `BROWSERSTACK_*` and
223	  the `E2E_*`/`PWA_E2E_*` vars in `.env` — see `.env.sample`. Manual, not enforced by a git
224	  hook — relies on developer discipline, not a blocking gate.
225	
226	### Multi-region fixtures
227	
228	Build SITE_ID-keyed fixtures from day one — Zimmermann has 8 storefronts across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME) and 11 active locales. Do not retrofit. A test that hardcodes a region or currency cannot survive the rollout.
229	
230	```ts
231	test.describe('Guest checkout', () => {
232	    for (const site of SITES) {
233	        test(`completes on ${site.id}`, async ({page}) => { ... })
234	    }
235	})
236	```
237	
238	### Page Object Model
239	
240	Selector priority — **enforce in code review**. Select elements the way real users (and assistive tech) perceive them:
241	
242	1. **Accessible selectors** — role with accessible name, label, placeholder, visible text. `getByRole('button', {name: 'Add to bag'})`, `getByLabelText('Email')`, `getByPlaceholderText('Search')`, `getByText('Sale')`. First choice — these double as continuous a11y checks.
243	2. **Semantic selectors** — standard HTML attributes when no accessible selector applies. `getByAltText('Profile picture')`, `getByTitle('Close modal')`.
244	3. **Test IDs** — `data-testid` only when the element has no semantic meaning or text content (dynamic containers, canvas elements, loading spinners, complex layout blocks).
245	
246	Never select by tag name, class name, or DOM position. The priority order keeps tests close to user experience and minimises `data-testid` clutter in the DOM, while still allowing a reliable fallback where semantics genuinely don't exist.
247	
248	### What NOT to write at this layer
249	
250	- Pure logic — that's Vitest
251	- Component interaction in isolation — that's Storybook `play`
252	- Network-mocked flows — Playwright always hits real SFCC APIs (dev org on feature PRs, SIT on the release gate). Do not stub network calls in Playwright tests.
253	
254	---
255	
256	## Test config files are Tier 1
257	
258	`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `lighthouserc.js` are
259	**frozen** ([frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)). Do not modify them in a feature PR — config drift breaks every contributor's harness. Changes go through the Integration team.
260	
261	---
262	
263	## Quick checklist before opening a PR
264	
265	- [ ] New component → has `*.stories.tsx`
266	- [ ] Non-obvious logic → has `*.test.ts`
267	- [ ] New user journey → has a `.feature` file (Playwright spec follows after Lead QA sign-off)
268	- [ ] `npm run test` passes locally
269	- [ ] No new MSW handlers in production-path code
270	- [ ] No edits to Tier 1 test config files
271

# Testing Conventions

Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.

**This is not license to skip a component's own test file because its behaviour happens to be
covered transitively elsewhere.** A component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping
decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx`, even when the state it
renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test, or a parent's assembly-level
Storybook `play` already exercises the rendered result. Resolve the duplication concern by
**scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven
elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract (given a state, does it render the
right branch; given a DOM event, does it call the right handler) — not by leaving the
component with no test of its own. Relying on a *different* component's story to prove *this*
component's contract means the coverage isn't discoverable from the component's own folder,
and can silently vanish if that unrelated file changes. See
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for the
resulting pattern (mocks `useSubscribeSection` and `ZimmSubscribeModal`, tests only its own
render-branch/event-wiring contract). A component with no branching or decision logic at all
(pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`) still doesn't need its own suite — the exemption
below for single-parent internal components still applies there.

| Layer | Tool | What it covers | File pattern | CI gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, hook behaviour in isolation | `*.test.ts` co-located with the source | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | User-facing interactions in a single component (clicks, form fills, focus management) | `*.stories.tsx` `play` function | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| E2E | Playwright | Full user journeys across pages, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,js}` | Every PR (`qa.yml`) — desktop + mobile Chromium against localhost/dev API; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**` only |

> Higher-level project rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing. Day-to-day file conventions: [conventions.md](./conventions.md). This file describes **how** to write tests at each layer.

---

## What to test (and what to skip)

Write tests where failure would be **non-obvious** or **costly to debug**:

- ✅ Data mapping: Contentful → component props, locale/currency transforms, SFCC payload → view model
- ✅ Integration boundaries: Global-e pricing/tax logic, checkout ownership branching, consent gating
- ✅ Complex state: cart mutations, consent state changes, multi-step flows, optimistic-update rollback
- ✅ Pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken
- ❌ Re-exports, one-line passthroughs, type-only helpers
- ❌ Storybook visual snapshots — Chromatic/Loki belongs in a separate budget, not Vitest
- ❌ The framework — don't test that React renders, that Chakra applies styles, or that React Query caches

---

## Layer 1 — Vitest (unit)

### File layout

Co-located with the source, `.test.ts` suffix, never `.spec.ts`:

```
overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.ts
overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.test.ts
overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.ts
overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.test.ts
```

Components use `index.test.ts` next to `index.tsx` in the component folder
(see [components.md](./components.md) > Components).

### Structure

- `describe` blocks group related cases; `test` (or `it`) for individual cases.
- **Arrange → Act → Assert** pattern, one behaviour per test.
- Test names describe the behaviour, not the implementation: `"converts AUD to USD using the latest Global-e rate"` not `"calls convertCurrency"`.
- Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test.

### Mocking

- **Inline mock objects** for isolated unit tests — define plain JS objects right in the test file.
- **`vi.mock()`** for module-level stubs. Mock the smallest possible surface: a single function, not a whole module, when feasible.
- **MSW** is allowed for cross-functional integration tests (multiple modules wired together). Production paths must never depend on MSW — see AGENTS.md > Rules > "No mocking."
- Do not mock the thing under test; do not assert on internal implementation calls when an output assertion would do.
- **Known gap: `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel
  (`app/components/icons`), which has a top-level side effect (`AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...`)
  that fails here because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings in this environment, not
  components. Not fixable from a test file — the SVG transform lives in `vitest.config.ts`,
  Tier 1 test config (AGENTS.md Hard Rule 8). Work around it by mocking `ZimmIcon` at the
  smallest surface in any test that renders an icon-consuming component:
  `vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))` — or,
  if an assertion depends on an accessible name the real `ZimmIcon` would carry (e.g. a
  fallback `<span aria-label>` with no wrapping interactive element), forward the relevant
  props instead of returning `null`. See `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` and
  `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for both variants.

### Commerce SDK hooks

Hooks that call `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (e.g. `useCurrentBasket`, `useCurrentCustomer`) need a `QueryClientProvider` and `CommerceApiProvider` wrapper. Build a small `renderWithProviders` helper in `overrides/app/test-utils/` rather than duplicating wrapper boilerplate per test.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Visual rendering — that's Storybook
- Cross-page navigation — that's Playwright
- Real network calls — never; use MSW or stubbed hooks

---

## Layer 2 — Storybook `play` (component interaction)

### When to use `play`

Every UI component has a `*.stories.tsx` (see [components.md](./components.md) > Storybook). Add a `play` function when there is **interactive behaviour worth asserting**:

- Form validation triggers on blur / submit
- Disclosure (accordion, drawer, modal) opens / closes via keyboard + mouse
- Focus moves correctly through a flow
- A controlled input's onChange wires through to the rendered output

If the story is purely visual (renders different prop combinations), no `play` is needed.

### Pattern

```tsx
import {expect, userEvent, within} from '@storybook/test'

export const SubmitDisabledUntilValid: Story = {
    play: async ({canvasElement}) => {
        const canvas = within(canvasElement)
        const submit = canvas.getByRole('button', {name: /submit/i})
        await expect(submit).toBeDisabled()
        await userEvent.type(canvas.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'name@example.com')
        await expect(submit).toBeEnabled()
    }
}
```

- Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly.
- Use **`getByRole`** with an accessible name as the first-choice selector. Fall back to `getByLabelText` for form fields, `getByText` last.
- Don't import `userEvent` from `@testing-library/user-event` — use the Storybook re-export so the action is logged in the timeline.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Multi-page flows — that's Playwright
- Heavy API mocking — keep stories visual, push integration assertions to Playwright

---

## Layer 3 — Playwright (E2E)

### Workflow

E2E tests follow the **three-stage gherkin-first workflow** (see [.claude/skills/qa-generate/](../skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md)):

1. Claude (or any developer) drafts a `.feature` file with Gherkin scenarios
2. Lead QA validates in plain English — **no Playwright code is written until sign-off**
3. Playwright spec is generated only after the `.feature` is approved

This prevents "technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour."

### File layout

```
e2e/features/         # Gherkin .feature files — source of truth, reviewed by Lead QA
e2e/fixtures/         # multi-region fixtures keyed by SITE_ID
e2e/support/
  helpers/            # shared helpers (auth, basket setup)
  pages/              # Page Object Model classes (BasePage, CheckoutPage, …)
e2e/tests/zimm/       # generated Playwright specs, mirroring features/
```

Spec filename convention for story-backed specs: `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`
(`.p0.` runs in the Digital SIT gate on `release/**`; on a `develop`-targeted PR, `e2e-localhost`
runs only the specs relevant to the diff — see **Change-scoped E2E** below). Jira-less smoke
tests use `SMOKE-{area}-{behaviour}.spec.js` instead — see
[e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests.

### Change-scoped E2E (`develop`-targeted PRs only)

`e2e-localhost` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) narrows which specs it runs based on the changed
files in the diff, instead of always running the full suite:

- Every spec must carry a Playwright test tag matching its Gherkin file's `@area` tag (see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) for the tag list — `homepage`,
  `checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations`) — and, per **BrowserStack story
  scoping** below, its `@SFCC-NNN` tag too: `test('...', {tag: ['@homepage', '@SFCC-142']}, async
  ({page}) => {...})`. Smoke tests (no Jira story — see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests) are exempt from the
  `@SFCC-NNN` half of this — `@area @smoke` only.
- `detect-changes`'s `Get changed files` step defines one file-path allow-list per area
  (`e2e_homepage`, and so on as new areas get specs). `Compute E2E scope` narrows the run to
  that area's `--grep` tag **only if every e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that one
  area's allow-list** — a single file outside it (a shared/global path, or one no area has
  claimed yet) falls back to the full suite, deliberately, rather than needing its own
  deny-list to maintain. `qa.yml`'s inline comments are the source of truth for the exact path
  lists — don't duplicate them here, they'll drift.
- `release/**`-targeted PRs always run the full suite regardless of diff — this narrowing only
  applies to `develop`-targeted PRs.
- **Adding a new area's first spec:** give it its own allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s
  `detect-changes` job, tag every `test()` in it with the matching `{tag: '@area'}`, and add it
  to this section. Forgetting either step doesn't lose coverage — an untagged/unmapped spec
  still runs under the full-suite fallback — it just misses out on the scoping optimisation.

### BrowserStack story scoping

`e2e-browserstack` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a
general regression gate — that's what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for.

- **`release/**`-targeted PRs:** always run the full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite, unscoped. A
  release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply — Zephyr
  traceability still works, since every test carries its own `@SFCC-NNN` tag individually.
- **`develop`-targeted PRs:** `detect-changes`'s `Detect Jira story keys` step regexes
  `SFCC-\d+` out of the PR title, PR body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-
  Jira app uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own. If
  at least one key is found, `e2e-browserstack` runs `--grep`-scoped to that story's tag(s)
  (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job doesn't run at
  all.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results to in Zephyr, there's
  nothing correct to run.
- If a key is found but no spec carries the matching `@SFCC-NNN` tag, `--grep` matches zero
  tests and Playwright reports "no tests found" without spinning up any BrowserStack sessions
  — a free no-op, not a failure, and not something that falls back to a full run.
- Every story-backed spec needs its Jira key as a tag alongside its `@area` tag (see
  **Change-scoped E2E** above) for this to work — the `qa-generate` skill adds both
  automatically. Jira-less smoke tests (`@area @smoke` only) never match a story key, so they
  correctly never run under BrowserStack — that's expected, not a gap; they're already covered
  by `e2e-localhost`.
- **Local pre-push equivalent:** `npm run test:story` (`scripts/runStoryTests.sh`) runs the
  same `browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep` command against real
  BrowserStack, so a developer can exercise their story before opening the PR. Pass the key
  explicitly (`npm run test:story -- SFCC-142`) or let it auto-detect from commit messages on
  the branch and the branch name — the same `SFCC-\d+` pattern, applied to local git state
  instead of PR title/body since no PR exists yet at that point. Requires `BROWSERSTACK_*` and
  the `E2E_*`/`PWA_E2E_*` vars in `.env` — see `.env.sample`. Manual, not enforced by a git
  hook — relies on developer discipline, not a blocking gate.

### Multi-region fixtures

Build SITE_ID-keyed fixtures from day one — Zimmermann has 8 storefronts across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME) and 11 active locales. Do not retrofit. A test that hardcodes a region or currency cannot survive the rollout.

```ts
test.describe('Guest checkout', () => {
    for (const site of SITES) {
        test(`completes on ${site.id}`, async ({page}) => { ... })
    }
})
```

### Page Object Model

Selector priority — **enforce in code review**. Select elements the way real users (and assistive tech) perceive them:

1. **Accessible selectors** — role with accessible name, label, placeholder, visible text. `getByRole('button', {name: 'Add to bag'})`, `getByLabelText('Email')`, `getByPlaceholderText('Search')`, `getByText('Sale')`. First choice — these double as continuous a11y checks.
2. **Semantic selectors** — standard HTML attributes when no accessible selector applies. `getByAltText('Profile picture')`, `getByTitle('Close modal')`.
3. **Test IDs** — `data-testid` only when the element has no semantic meaning or text content (dynamic containers, canvas elements, loading spinners, complex layout blocks).

Never select by tag name, class name, or DOM position. The priority order keeps tests close to user experience and minimises `data-testid` clutter in the DOM, while still allowing a reliable fallback where semantics genuinely don't exist.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Pure logic — that's Vitest
- Component interaction in isolation — that's Storybook `play`
- Network-mocked flows — Playwright always hits real SFCC APIs (dev org on feature PRs, SIT on the release gate). Do not stub network calls in Playwright tests.

---

## Test config files are Tier 1

`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `lighthouserc.js` are
**frozen** ([frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)). Do not modify them in a feature PR — config drift breaks every contributor's harness. Changes go through the Integration team.

---

## Quick checklist before opening a PR

- [ ] New component → has `*.stories.tsx`
- [ ] Non-obvious logic → has `*.test.ts`
- [ ] New user journey → has a `.feature` file (Playwright spec follows after Lead QA sign-off)
- [ ] `npm run test` passes locally
- [ ] No new MSW handlers in production-path code
- [ ] No edits to Tier 1 test config files
